Waluigi suspects the wand is more confused by Bowser than Bowser is by the wand.

## Relationship with Disaster Inc.

Bowser's alliance with Disaster Inc. is one of the most unlikely partnerships in the campaign. Bowser is traditionally an ANTAGONIST—kidnapping princesses, conquering kingdoms, generally being the obstacle that heroes overcome.

But the Planar Fracture threw normal alignments into chaos. Bowser ended up on the same side as the party because the SITUATION demanded it. Vampires don't care about Mushroom Kingdom politics. The Shadowfell doesn't distinguish between heroes and villains. When everyone is trapped in a death dimension together, old rivalries become irrelevant and shared survival becomes paramount.

Bowser has adapted to this alliance with surprising grace. He follows Markop's tactical suggestions—not because he recognizes Markop's authority, but because Markop's suggestions are usually GOOD and Bowser respects competence even if he'd never admit it.

Waluigi finds this unexpectedly endearing. Bowser, the great villain, taking direction from a lizardfolk tactician because the alternative is dying in a vampire's hallway. Circumstances make strange allies.

## Assessment

Bowser is not the most skilled fighter in Disaster Inc. He's not the most magical or the most tactical or the most politically savvy.

Bowser is the most INDESTRUCTIBLE.

He takes hits that would kill anyone else and keeps fighting. He faces threats that would terrify anyone else and keeps punching. He finds necromantic artifacts in death dimensions and asks if they're magic wands with the curiosity of someone browsing a gift shop.

Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser. Waluigi LOST, which Waluigi attributes to the table being at the wrong height and NOT to any deficiency in Waluigi's arm strength, which is CONSIDERABLE.

But Waluigi respects Bowser. In a crisis, Waluigi wants Bowser nearby. Not for subtlety—Bowser doesn't DO subtlety. For SURVIVAL. Because when everything goes wrong and the death beams are flying, Bowser will hold the door, drag you to safety, hit the attacker in the head, and then find something interesting on the floor.

That's not elegance. That's RELIABILITY. And in the Shadow Estate right now, reliability might be worth more than anything.

WAH.

name: Valorian Stormweave
title: The Dead Man Who Took His Secrets With Him
status: Deceased — killed by Archie Miser in a public market, 1040 BF. Ruled 'justifiable magical defense' by Onyx Hand tribunal.
summary: Valorian Stormweave was a Senior Enforcer of the Mages' Guild who—according to Lady Bloomia's testimony—was present at the Royal Vault on the morning of Princess Peach's assassination in 955 BF. He allegedly delayed the Solstice Crown delivery, knew Bloomia's name without introduction, smiled 'like a predator who has confirmed the location of its prey,' and was part of the Guild's involvement in 'the arrangement.' He lived for eighty-five years after allegedly helping murder a princess. Then Archie Miser killed him in a public market during an altercation that an Onyx Hand tribunal ruled justifiable. The only person who could have testified about Guild complicity in the assassination is now ash. Whether this is cosmic justice, cosmic irony, or cosmic convenience depends entirely on who you ask—and EVERYONE has an opinion. Waluigi has spent considerable time examining this death because it sits at the intersection of two stories that should have nothing to do with each other: Archie's chaotic journey and the eighty-five-year-old assassination conspiracy. The intersection is either coincidence or something much worse. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Valorian Stormweave with the acknowledgment that most of what Waluigi knows about this man comes from two sources: Lady Bloomia's testimony (which may or may not be authentic) and the public record of his death at Archie Miser's hands (which is documented but contextually complicated). Between these two data points lies eighty-five years of a life Waluigi knows almost nothing about—a career in the Mages' Guild, a rise to Senior Enforcer, and whatever private knowledge he carried about one particular morning in 955 BF.

## The Morning of Highsun 1, 955 BF — Bloomia's Account

If Lady Bloomia's testimony is authentic—and Waluigi must emphasize the IF, because the Regency disputes Bloomia's entire existence—then Valorian Stormweave was present at the Royal Vault on the morning Princess Peach was assassinated.

Bloomia describes encountering two figures in dark robes embroidered with silver staves—Mages' Guild identification—arguing with the vault master Cornelius about 'unauthorized magical access' to the Solstice Crown's seals.

The taller mage was silver-haired, pale-eyed, with 'the particular condescension that the Guild cultivates like a hothouse flower.' He was DELAYING the crown delivery. The vault master insisted the seals were intact. The mage insisted Guild instruments detected irregularities. The crown could not be released until their 'investigation' was complete.

Then Bloomia arrived. The Princess had sent her to retrieve the crown personally.

The tall mage turned. He looked through Bloomia 'the way mages look through anyone who cannot cast.' Then he said her name.

'The handmaiden. Bloomia, yes?'

He KNEW her name. Without introduction. Without being told. A Senior Guild Enforcer knew the name of a seventeen-year-old handmaiden he had supposedly never met.

He then asked questions that demonstrated knowledge of what was happening in the Princess's chambers: 'Have you noticed anything unusual? Visitors at odd hours? Passages that seem to lead nowhere? Smells that don't belong?'

He was describing EXACTLY what Bloomia had observed that morning—the earth-and-pine smell of Thornpaw's visits, the shifted cushions, the passages Peach kept sending Bloomia away from. He KNEW about the secret visitor. He knew about the hatch.

Bloomia lied. 'No. Nothing unusual.'

He smiled. The smile of a predator who has confirmed the location of its prey.

'Of course not. Well, take the crown. We were just leaving.'

They stepped aside. Bloomia took the crown and ran.

As she ran, the tall mage called after her: 'Be careful, Bloomia. The wards have been behaving strangely today. Fluctuations in the protective enchantments.'

He was WARNING her. Not out of kindness—out of cruelty. He wanted her to know that something was happening and that she could not stop it. The wards were 'fluctuating' because the Guild was DISABLING them. The protective enchantments around the Princess's chambers were being deliberately weakened.

The tall mage was Valorian Stormweave.

## The Encoded Field Note — Guild Awareness

Bloomia later found a notation scratched into the vault's visitor log in a Guild field cipher—a number-substitution code that translates to:

'SUBJECT IS AWARE. THE HATCH IS OPEN. PROCEED AS PLANNED.'

This note—if authentic—confirms that the Guild knew about the secret hatch, knew the assassination was proceeding, and was coordinating their actions around the timeline. 'Subject is aware' likely refers to Peach herself, who had told Bloomia she knew something was coming.

Stormweave's presence at the vault was not coincidence. He was there to DELAY the crown delivery—keeping Bloomia away from the Royal Suite during the killing window. He was there to CONFIRM that the operation was on schedule. He was there to ensure that the Guild's piece of 'the arrangement' was executed with bureaucratic precision.

## The Eighty-Five Years — What Did Stormweave Know?

Valor Stormweave lived for eighty-five years after the assassination.

EIGHTY-FIVE YEARS.

He rose to the rank of Senior Enforcer within the Mages' Guild—a position of significant authority and institutional trust. He operated within the Guild's power structure for decades, presumably continuing to serve the organization that Bloomia accuses of facilitating the Princess's murder.

What did he know during those eighty-five years?

Did he know the identity of the assassin? He was in the vault that morning. He knew about the hatch. He knew the operation was 'proceeding as planned.' The Guild 'provided the method,' according to Toadsworth Sr.'s journals. Stormweave may have known WHO held the blade as well as who opened the door.

Did he know where the evidence went? The Guild took control of all 'magical evidence' after the assassination. What they collected, what they destroyed, what they concealed—Stormweave, as a Senior Enforcer, would have had access to classified operational records.

Did he know about Lady Bloomia? Guild operatives hunted Bloomia through the servant passages within hours of the assassination. One of them died when the Silent One intervened. Stormweave may have been involved in ordering that pursuit—or at least aware of it.

Did he know about Mario's 'reallocation'? If the Guild cooperated with the Regency to remove Mario before the assassination and to suppress his investigation afterward, Stormweave may have known the details—where Mario was sent, what happened to him, why he disappeared.

Every secret of the assassination conspiracy—every name on Peach's list, every detail of the arrangement, every piece of suppressed evidence—was potentially accessible to Valorian Stormweave for eighty-five years.

And then Archie Miser killed him in a market.

## The Death — Archie's Market Fight

The circumstances of Stormweave's death in 1040 BF are documented in the Onyx Hand's tribunal records:

Archie Miser and Valorian Stormweave were involved in an altercation in a public market. The altercation escalated to magical violence. Archie killed Stormweave. The Onyx Hand tribunal that examined the case ruled it 'justifiable magical defense.'

The specifics of what triggered the altercation are not extensively documented in Waluigi's sources. Market confrontations between mages can escalate for any number of reasons—territorial disputes, personal grudges, accidental magical interference, or simply two volatile personalities occupying the same space.

What matters is not the cause but the CONSEQUENCE: the one person who could have testified about Guild involvement in the assassination is dead.

## The Coincidence Problem — Was It Really Random?

Waluigi must address the uncomfortable question: was Stormweave's death actually a random market fight?

Arguments for coincidence:

**Archie didn't know.** There is no evidence that Archie knew who Stormweave was or what he had done eighty-five years ago. Archie was born long after the assassination. He had no connection to the conspiracy investigation. He had no reason to target Stormweave specifically.

**Market fights happen.** Mages argue. Arguments escalate. People die. This is not unusual in a kingdom that has been at war for eighty-five years.

**The tribunal ruled justifiable defense.** If Archie attacked Stormweave unprovoked, the tribunal would not have ruled in his favor. The ruling suggests Stormweave was the aggressor or at least equally responsible for the escalation.

Arguments against coincidence:

**The timing.** Stormweave survived eighty-five years. He was killed in 1040 BF—the same year that the assassination conspiracy began to unravel. Thornpaw was about to confirm the secret relationship at Fawful's gala. The Loyalists were closing in on the truth. Stormweave was becoming a liability.

**Who benefits?** The Guild benefits from Stormweave's death. The one person who could testify about their involvement is silenced permanently. No interrogation. No testimony. No accountability.

**Archie's entropy.** The Mages' Guild later described Archie's magic as 'bleeding entropy'—destabilizing reality around him. What if Archie was ATTRACTED to Stormweave—or Stormweave to Archie—through dimensional resonance? What if the market encounter was not random but INEVITABLE, caused by planar forces that brought entropy and conspiracy into collision?

**Guild manipulation.** The Guild subsequently employed Archie. They knew about his capabilities. They knew about his instability. What if the market encounter was ARRANGED—the Guild engineering a confrontation between their most dangerous secret-keeper and a volatile mage who would eliminate the problem without knowing he was doing the Guild's work?

Waluigi cannot determine whether the death was coincidence or conspiracy. Both explanations have problems. Neither is fully satisfying.

What Waluigi CAN say: the death is CONVENIENT. Convenient deaths should always be examined carefully. And the convenience benefits the Mages' Guild more than any other party.

## Bloomia's Response — A Debt Unknowingly Owed

Lady Bloomia—if she exists, if her testimony is authentic—added a note to her manuscript about Stormweave's death:

'Valorian Stormweave lived for eighty-five more years after helping murder my Princess. He was eventually killed by a mage named Archie Miser in a public market—"justifiable magical defense," the Onyx Hand ruled. I do not know Archie Miser. But I owe him a debt he will never know about.'

Then she added:

'The only man who could have testified about what the Guild knew that morning is now ash. Convenient. Very convenient.'

Bloomia sees the same pattern Waluigi sees. The witness is dead. The testimony is lost. The Guild's secrets died with the man who kept them.

Bloomia owes Archie a debt. Archie doesn't know the debt exists. He killed a man in a market fight and has no idea that the man he killed was the last living link to the assassination of Princess Peach.

The cosmic irony is STAGGERING. Archie—the walking disaster, the entropy-bleeder, the man who resolves everything with fireballs—accidentally destroyed the most important piece of evidence in an eighty-five-year-old murder investigation. Not through malice. Not through intention. Through the same chaotic violence that defines everything Archie touches.

Archie Miser: solving and destroying mysteries simultaneously, one fireball at a time.

## What Died With Stormweave — The Lost Testimony

The knowledge that Valorian Stormweave took to his grave:

**The Guild's exact role.** How many Guild operatives were involved? Who gave the orders? What specific actions did the Guild take—disabling wards, providing the assassination method, hunting Bloomia, suppressing evidence?

**The assassin's identity.** Stormweave was at the vault. He knew the hatch was open. He knew the operation was proceeding. He may have known who walked through that hatch with a blade.

**The evidence disposition.** The Guild took control of all magical evidence from the crime scene. What they found, what they kept, what they destroyed—Stormweave would have known.

**The ongoing cover-up.** Eighty-five years of institutional secrecy. Who participated? Who was compromised? What documents exist in sealed Guild archives that could expose the conspiracy?

**Mario's situation.** If the Guild was involved in Mario's 'reallocation' after his investigation threatened the cover-up, Stormweave may have known the details—where Mario was sent, who authorized it, what leverage was used.

All of this knowledge is gone. Destroyed in a market fight by a man who had no idea what he was destroying.

Unless Stormweave left records. Unless he wrote things down. Unless he told someone. Unless there are Guild archives somewhere that contain his personal files, his operational logs, his private notes.

The Mages' Guild does not discard records easily. They are BUREAUCRATS. They document everything. If Stormweave's knowledge exists in written form somewhere—in a sealed vault, in a classified archive, in the kind of institutional memory that organizations preserve against future need—then his death did not destroy the evidence. It merely made it harder to access.

Waluigi intends to pursue this line of investigation. The Guild keeps records. Records can be found. And somewhere in the Mages' Guild's archives, eighty-five years of Valorian Stormweave's career are documented in forms, reports, and classified files that may contain the truth about the morning Princess Peach was murdered.

Finding those records is now on Waluigi's list. Near the top.

Right after escaping the Feywild.

Right after the tennis match with Mario.

WAH.

name: Toad Lee
title: The Defenestrated Diplomat
status: Active — Exploring the Overgrown Manor
summary: Toad Lee continues to be the only reason Disaster Inc. hasn't been completely consumed by the Feywild. He reads the lore, manages the incredibly drunk Rakasha, and initiates combat when necessary. He recently survived being thrown out of a high-story window by a goblin guard, which Waluigi finds highly amusing but respects the commitment to the fight.
description:
Toad Lee is proving to be a surprisingly aggressive diplomat. While he initially served as the quiet, observant foil to Waluigi's loud magnificence, the Feywild is wearing on him.

**The Combat Pragmatist**
When Remi's mechanical dog was stolen by goblin servants looking for scrap metal, Toad Lee didn't bother with fey riddles. He barged into the servant's quarters (interrupting a goblin on the toilet) and demanded the dog back. In the ensuing sword fight, Toad Lee's shield was stolen by the guard Gregory. Toad Lee attempted a heroic acrobatic maneuver, failed spectacularly, and fell out the window. He was only saved because Azure manifested a spectral hand to catch him.

**The Lore Keeper**
While Hjumpik is busy throwing axes at bombs, Toad Lee is actually paying attention to the environment. He uncovered Lady Aurelian's diary, reading critical lore about 'The Grafting' and the arrival of the Iron Legion. Toad Lee is the brain of the Feywild operation, even if his acrobatic skills need serious work. Waluigi will offer him tennis lessons if they survive this.

## Expanded Waluipedia Notes

Toad Lee is the kind of character who becomes important because everyone else is too busy being dramatic. He listens. He reads. He notices the diary on the shelf while stronger people argue about which door to kick. In the Feywild operation, this is not a minor talent. The Feyward punishes people who treat lore as decoration. Toad Lee treats lore as equipment, which makes him more valuable than several people carrying actual equipment.

His failures are also instructive. The window incident proves he is not a flawless operative, but Waluigi does not require flawless operatives. Waluigi requires useful ones. Toad Lee's usefulness is quiet, cumulative, and easy to undervalue until the moment everyone realizes the only reason they understand the room is because he read the thing nobody else wanted to read. WAH.

name: Ryan
title: The Man Who Jumped
status: Active — location uncertain, last known contact with Rakasha spirit-walkers
summary: Ryan is the person who jumped off the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach rather than be captured by the Iron Legion. He jumped. Off an airship. In the sky. He survived—somehow—and was taken in by a Rakasha spirit-walker. Waluigi does not know Ryan's current status or location, but anyone who survives a jump like that has earned Waluigi's respect forever.
description:
Waluigi was not aboard the Vigilance when the Iron Legion boarded and captured it. He learned about Ryan's escape secondhand, and the account makes his stomach clench every time he thinks about it.

Ryan was cornered on the observation deck. Iron Legion troops closing from two directions. No exit except the door they were coming through and the railing behind him. Most people, in that situation, would surrender. Most people would calculate the odds—capture versus certain death—and choose capture.

Ryan jumped.

## The Jump

Waluigi needs to emphasize how INSANE this decision was. The Vigilance was flying. The drop to the ground was... Waluigi doesn't actually know how far, but it was FAR ENOUGH that surviving should have been impossible. Physics says you die. Biology says you die. Basic common sense says you die.

Ryan jumped anyway.

Something about the angle of descent, the air currents, hitting tree canopy in a way that distributed the impact across multiple surfaces—Ryan survived. Injured but alive. Waluigi does not fully understand the mechanics. Waluigi suspects Ryan doesn't either. What matters is that Ryan chose certain death over uncertain captivity and somehow found a third option that nobody knew existed.

Waluigi has been in desperate situations before. He has faced enemies, monsters, fairy courts, and mirror dimensions. He does not know if he would have the courage to jump off an airship with no guarantee of survival. He does not know if that's courage or desperation or something else entirely. What he knows is that Ryan did it, and Ryan lived, and that makes Ryan one of the bravest people Waluigi has ever encountered.

## The Rakasha Spirit-Walker

After the jump, Ryan was found by a Rakasha spirit-walker—a being associated with spiritual traditions and dimensional sensitivities that Waluigi does not have extensive knowledge of. The spirit-walker took Ryan in, treated his injuries, and... then what? Waluigi does not know. Ryan's thread diverged from the main narrative of the crisis at that point.

The Rakasha connection is intriguing. Spirit-walkers presumably have knowledge of dimensional boundaries, planar transitions, and the kind of metaphysical mechanics that might be relevant to repairing the Planar Fracture. Whether Ryan's encounter with the spirit-walker was coincidence or something more deliberate, Waluigi cannot say.

## Assessment

Ryan is out there somewhere. Separated from the rest of Disaster Inc., possibly learning things from Rakasha spirit-walkers, possibly preparing to rejoin the fight. Waluigi hopes he's healing. Waluigi hopes he's gathering strength. And Waluigi hopes that when the party reunites—and they WILL reunite, Waluigi refuses to accept otherwise—Ryan comes back with whatever wisdom or power the spirit-walkers have to offer.

Anyone who jumps off an airship and survives deserves to come back as something MORE than they were before. That's just narrative justice. WAH.

name: Bones
title: The Infiltrator Who Triggered the Massacre & Master of the Planar Sanctum Discovery
race: Unknown (skilled at disguise, so identification is uncertain)
status: Active — resting at an Alpine Mountain Inn near Midgrual/Regal Capital after escaping the Planar Sanctum, meeting the Toad God, and discovering Thornbury's betrayal
summary: Bones is a master infiltrator who survived Aegis Command, Order 120, and custody in the Corvinarus Planar Sanctum. After awakening alone in the Fractured Sanctum, Bones stole Fundamentals of Abjuration, uncovered Corvinarus's 10-page masterwork Veins of the Tapestry, refused the Oracle's flesh vat, engaged a fiendish Canoloth, was saved by the Toad God at the Astral Altar, and was teleported to the Regal Capital. There, at Alpine Bank, Bones eavesdropped on Thornbury placing a bounty on Archie Miser over a broken rope and claiming Legion credentials. Bones fled into a severe snowstorm and paid 3 Midland Ducats for shelter at an Alpine Inn.
description:
Waluigi has to write about Bones carefully because Bones has lived through enough history to fill three separate war tribunals and still manages to walk into rooms nobody knew existed.

Originally one of the most capable operatives among the Liberated Toads, Bones achieved legend status by passing as an Iron Legion soldier inside Aegis Command for days. His capture triggered Order 120—the administrative execution of every Toad in Legion custody—a weight he has carried quietly ever since. But his story did not end in General Ironhand's interrogation room.

## Awakening in the Planar Sanctum
Following the shattered synchronization attempt with Archie Miser, Bones woke up alone on the black marble floor of the Planar Sanctum. Finding himself separated from Archie and wondering where Orange T had gone, Bones remembered Thornbury Bones and began exploring the crumbling complex. In the library, he spotted *Fundamentals of Abjuration*—a Mages' Guild Conservator text—and stole it directly from the Oracle's shelves, remarking he'd keep it when he found free time.

## Reading the Veins of the Tapestry
Near the scattered debris of a ruined grand turret—where a fallen belfry bell lay smashed against black marble—Bones found a second tome on the floor: *Veins of the Tapestry: A Record of Threads Severed and Mended*. Written in the precise, arrogant hand of Corvinarus, the pages whispered into his skull under the rippling light of nearby vats:

- **Page 1:** Dedication 'To the three who will break what we bound' signed with three interlocking threads (one frayed).
- **Page 2:** Architectural diagram of pre-Fracture Raventree Manor with mirror and shadow weak points.
- **Page 3:** Account of the 988 BF Grafting ritual, describing the egg's scream as 'the sound of a future being forced into existence.'
- **Page 4:** Warning about the Oracle (OC): 'pulls levers she does not fully understand... vats were never meant to birth keepers.'
- **Page 5:** List of test subjects from Orangus Cornelius to Vivian ('He laughs when cut. This was not planned.').
- **Page 6:** Circle repair instructions (bone ash, live wood, iron dust, chalk) and doodle of a three-eyed figure: 'Do not trust the fire that cannot burn.'
- **Page 7:** Shadowfell lament: 'Orangus believed order could contain the bleed... The Hand feeds what it claims to control.'
- **Page 8:** Pressed glowing Feywild flower with Lady Aurelian's warning: 'the present must be severed from the others or all will unravel like cheap silk.'
- **Page 9:** Map of Deep Mirror sanctum labeling abomination vats as 'Failed attempts at continuity' with 'Wrong lever' underlined three times.
- **Page 10:** Prophecy fragment: 'When the one-armed shadow walks with the fire that bleeds, and the green one takes the children's table, the threads will knot or snap. Choose the knot.'

## Confrontation with the Oracle & Flesh Vat Refusal
Hiding in turret rubble after hearing footsteps, Bones was confronted from behind by the Oracle. Apprehensive, Bones asked where they stood. The Oracle reprimanded Bones for failing to kill rival Oracles over the past two months and warned him never to touch his books. In the central chamber—flanked by Western violet and Eastern erratic orange Crystal Tethers surrounding a glass vat wrapped in lightning—the Oracle urged Bones into a flesh vat to reveal his 'true self-reflection.' Recognizing the red flag, Bones refused. When an unseen portal opened and Bones attempted to flee, the Oracle force-dragged him back.

## Combat with the Canoloth & The Astral Altar
A fiendish Canoloth appeared among floating space-time rocks. As the Oracle used a vibrating tuning fork to shift the beast in and out of reality, the Canoloth attacked Bones, snaring him with its spiny tongue and entangling both his longsword and vile mace. In agony, Bones grabbed the creature's tongue bare-handed, dragging the multi-ton yugoloth toward a cliff edge while demanding to kill it 'the actual way.' The Canoloth swiped Bones across the chest, knocking him unconscious.

Bones's mind was intercepted to the Astral Altar, where the Toad God (Mad Toad) greeted him as a 'best friend.' The Toad God advised Bones: 'Don't kill the Oracle, keep him alive. Leave the manor and crystal shard intact and leave it divided.' The Toad God mentioned being kept busy by 'pesky star bears wanting to give away their stars to a bunch of hooligans (the Oracle)' before a blinding light returned Bones to the sanctum floor.

The Oracle healed Bones, lecturing him that physical weightlifting won't grant strength if his mental reflex is to flee rather than fight. Agreeing to teleport Bones to a 'friend,' the Oracle placed him in a red circle pointed toward Alpine Bank.

## Eavesdropping at Alpine Bank & The Mountain Snowstorm
Materializing at Alpine Bank in the mountains near Midgrual (the Regal Capital), Bones met Thornbury. Lingering outside to eavesdrop on Thornbury's session with the Alpine banker, Bones learned:
- Thornbury operates with Iron Legion credentials and serves higher Legion commanders.
- The Legion considers Bones a wanted criminal for allegedly 'strangling a toad to death on the Vigilance.'
- Thornbury placed an official bounty on Archie Miser to collect 2,062 gold for the broken hempen rope debt.

Realizing Thornbury was a traitor, Bones quietly slipped out into a brewing mountain snowstorm. Freezing in the blizzard, he was escorted by local guards to an Alpine Inn, where he paid 3 Midland Ducats (3 gold) for a room upstairs, keeping a watchful eye for spies as he collapsed into bed.

name: Earl Grey
title: The Man Who Exploded
status: Deceased — literally exploded during the Syndicate Showdown
summary: Earl Grey was the primary enforcer for the Tea Leaf Syndicate—a skilled fighter whose loyalty to Green T was matched only by his combat effectiveness. His death during the Syndicate Showdown was the single most dramatic exit Waluigi has ever witnessed: Roger's poisoned dagger interacted with something in Earl Grey's biology, and the man DETONATED. Waluigi's favorite hat was in the blast radius. Waluigi is still upset about the hat.
description:
Earl Grey was the Tea Leaf Syndicate's muscle—the person who handled problems that couldn't be solved with tea and conversation. While Green T maintained the Syndicate's refined image, Earl Grey enforced its will with the kind of physical capability that made people reconsider disagreeing with the organization.

Waluigi did not know Earl Grey well. Their interactions were limited to the tense period between the Tea Party Incident and the Syndicate Showdown, when the Syndicate was hemorrhaging power and Earl Grey was fighting desperately to preserve what remained. Waluigi respected his determination even while recognizing that the Syndicate was already doomed.

## Combat Capabilities

Earl Grey was, by all accounts, one of the best pure fighters aboard the Vigilance. He moved with efficiency that suggested extensive training, engaged multiple opponents simultaneously without apparent strain, and possessed physical capabilities that exceeded what his frame would suggest. During the Syndicate Showdown, he held his own against several attackers at once, buying time for Green T to do... whatever Green T was planning.

The fight might have gone differently if the poison hadn't intervened.

## The Explosion

Roger's poisoned dagger struck Earl Grey during the melee. Under normal circumstances, the poison would have caused paralysis, unconsciousness, or death through conventional means. Earl Grey's physiology was not conventional.

The poison interacted with SOMETHING in Earl Grey's body chemistry. An alchemical compound in his blood? A latent magical instability? A mutation from years of sampling the Syndicate's more experimental tea blends? Nobody has ever adequately explained what happened or why. What Waluigi knows is the RESULT.

Earl Grey exploded.

Not figuratively. Not 'he was hit so hard he flew apart.' His body DETONATED. Outward. In all directions. The sound was somewhere between a thunderclap and a wet pop—a sound that Waluigi heard clearly and wishes he hadn't. People ten feet away were knocked off their feet. Items scattered across the marketplace. Biological matter went everywhere.

Waluigi's favorite hat was in the blast radius. The hat—custom made, carefully maintained, one of Waluigi's most treasured possessions—was SPLATTERED. By EARL GREY. Waluigi knows this is a petty concern compared to the death of a person, but the hat was IMPORTANT to Waluigi and he's allowed to grieve.

## Legacy

Earl Grey's death ended the Syndicate Showdown effectively. The remaining Syndicate members—those few who hadn't been killed by Archie's fireball days earlier—either surrendered or fled. Green T survived, but his organization died with Earl Grey's detonation.

The marketplace where Earl Grey exploded reportedly smelled strange for days afterward. Nobody could agree on what exactly the smell was—ozone, chemicals, something organic, something else. The uncertainty made it worse. Waluigi avoided that part of the Vigilance until the smell faded, and even then, he found himself checking the floor for... residue.

Waluigi does not know what to say about Earl Grey as a person. He was loyal to his organization, fought hard for it, and died in a way that nobody expected. His death was the exclamation point on the Tea Leaf Syndicate's collapse—a dramatic, horrible, unexplainable end that matched the dramatic, horrible, unexplainable events of the entire campaign.

Rest in pieces, Earl Grey. Waluigi means that LITERALLY. WAH.

name: Dan (The Parallel Paradox)
title: The Multi-Dimensional Headache
status: Active — Split between 'Original', 'Parallel', and 'Purple T'
summary: There are too many Dans. The cautious survivor Waluigi knew has been replaced by a dimensional duplicate. The 'Parallel Dan' traveling with Markop admitted he shoved the original Dan into a Mages' Guild null cage to silence him. Meanwhile, another Toad operative ('Purple T') is hunting Archie. Waluigi is deeply frustrated by this. One bureaucrat is annoying; a multiverse of bureaucrats is a nightmare.
description:
Waluigi must attempt to explain a situation that gives him a migraine. 

During a rest in the Shadowfell forest, Markop cast a Zone of Truth and confronted Dan. Dan confessed that he was NOT the original Dan. He is a 'Parallel Dan' from the mirror dimension. He swapped places with the original Dan during a restaurant raid weeks ago.

**The Fate of the Original**
Parallel Dan admitted he didn't kill the original Dan. Instead, he handed the original over to the Mages' Guild, who locked him in a 'null cage'—a magical containment unit that nullifies all arcane abilities. The original Dan is currently trapped in a Mages' Guild barrack, wearing an associate badge (Number 447) that tracks his movements and burns him if he tries to remove it. He is a prisoner disguised as an initiate, hiding coded notes in his mattress.

**The Motive**
Parallel Dan claims he disrupted the Oracle's ritual because if the ritual had succeeded, the parallel reality would have collapsed, killing him. He replaced the original to ensure his own survival. It is a selfish, cowardly act that perfectly aligns with Dan's core philosophy of survival at any cost. Even across dimensions, Dan is consistent.

**Purple T and the Rogue Mages**
To make matters infinitely worse, another operative known as 'Purple T' (who may or may not be another variant of Dan, or just a very sneaky Toad) has gone rogue. Purple T, along with a zealot named Bryan (servant of the 'Toad God'), ripped off their Mages' Guild tracking badges. They are currently hunting Archie Miser, using Archie's 'Wahbook' tablet posts to track his location across dimensions. 

Waluigi's assessment is simple: Trust no Toad named Dan. If you see a Dan, assume he is a spy, a clone, or about to lock you in a cage. WAH.

name: Eager
title: The Magnet for Catastrophe
status: Active — escaped the Shadow Estate rooftop with Remi’s Feather Fall after participating in the continuing Toad disaster chorus
summary:
Eager is the person whose rescue from the spider grove triggered the Battle of the Spider Grove. He has a supernatural gift for finding the worst possible place to be and BEING there. If there's a giant spider nest within ten miles, Eager will be inside it. If there's a bottomless pit, Eager will be sitting on its edge. Waluigi has mixed feelings about Eager—gratitude that rescuing him led to an excellent battle, frustration that the rescue was necessary in the first place.

Eager survived the rooftop escape sequence by remaining with Remi’s Feather Fall chain. He also remains implicated in the broader Toad tradition of turning stealth operations into songs, which Waluigi cannot legally prove is a crime but emotionally knows is one.
description:
Waluigi does not know how Eager ended up cocooned in the Silent Grove. Waluigi suspects even EAGER doesn't fully know how Eager ended up cocooned in the Silent Grove. What Waluigi knows is that when the party needed to mount a rescue operation, Eager was suspended fifteen feet off the ground between two dead oaks, wrapped in spider silk like the world's worst piñata.

This is TYPICAL for Eager.

## The Catastrophe Magnet Effect

Eager seems to attract dangerous situations the way Wario attracts coins. It's not that Eager SEEKS danger—he doesn't seem to have a death wish or a thrill-seeking personality. Danger just FINDS him. He walks into rooms and discovers they're on fire. He takes shortcuts that lead through forbidden territories. He sits down to rest and ends up in a spider queen's web.

Waluigi has met unlucky people before. Waluigi considers himself somewhat unlucky (though Waluigi believes his 'bad luck' is actually SYSTEMATIC UNFAIRNESS). But Eager's relationship with catastrophe exceeds normal unluckiness. It's almost supernatural. If Eager ever figures out how to CONTROL this effect—direct it at enemies instead of himself—he'd be one of the most dangerous people in the setting.

## The Rescue and After

The party rescued Eager from the spider grove through a multi-phase battle that included titan wrestling, arcane rays, exploding spiders, and a banishment circle. Eager, for his part, contributed by deploying pepper spray against clusters of smaller arachnids while stuck in an enlarged form.

Pepper spray. Against spiders. And it WORKED.

Waluigi has to give Eager credit for creative thinking. Most people, stuck in a giant form in the middle of a spider battle, would not think to use pepper spray. Eager apparently carries pepper spray into situations where pepper spray should be useless, and then finds situations where it becomes useful. This is either preparation or luck, and Waluigi cannot tell which.

## Assessment

Eager is an asset and a liability in equal measure. His tendency to end up in dangerous situations creates opportunities for dramatic battles and valuable loot (the Spider Grove yielded excellent items). It also creates rescue obligations that drain resources and attention.

Waluigi has decided to view Eager as a quest generator. Wherever Eager is, there's probably a problem. That problem probably has treasure attached. So following Eager is, in a weird way, a viable strategy for acquiring wealth and experience, as long as you're prepared to fight whatever horrible thing has captured Eager THIS time.

WAH.

## Recent Update — Feather Fall Escape

Eager was part of the group that grabbed onto Remi and descended safely from the roof while servants below sang We Are the Servants. Waluigi does not know why there is always singing. Waluigi only records that there is always singing.

name: Smoking J
title: The Venomous Casualty
status: Active — recovering from spider venom
summary: Smoking J was bitten during the Battle of the Spider Grove and suffered a severe venomous reaction that forced his withdrawal from the front line. His incapacitation at a critical moment reduced the party's fighting strength during the most dangerous phase of the battle. Waluigi hopes Smoking J has fully recovered, though the long-term effects of arachnid venom are unpredictable.
description:
Smoking J was an active combatant during Phase 2 of the Spider Grove battle—the period when the grove's defenses were fracturing and smaller arachnids were converging from all directions. He was fighting alongside the main group when one of the dog-sized spiders landed a bite.

The venom hit FAST. Swelling. Disorientation. The kind of systemic reaction that says 'this biological agent does not belong in your body and your body knows it.' Smoking J had to be pulled back from the front line, reducing the party's combat strength at exactly the wrong moment.

## Impact on the Battle

Smoking J's incapacitation was one of several factors that made the Spider Grove battle so desperate. With Smoking J down, the remaining fighters had to cover more ground with fewer people. The toad squad got cut off partly because there weren't enough fighters to maintain a continuous line. Remi had to hold her position with only her mechanical dog as backup.

Waluigi is not assigning blame—Smoking J didn't CHOOSE to be bitten, and arachnid venom is not something you can shrug off through determination. But the tactical consequences of his withdrawal rippled through the rest of the engagement.

## Recovery

Waluigi does not know Smoking J's current status. The Planar Fracture scattered the party before Waluigi could confirm whether the venom's effects had fully resolved. Arachnid venoms are unpredictable—some cause immediate effects that fade quickly, others linger in the system for days or weeks, and some leave permanent damage.

Waluigi hopes Smoking J is fully recovered. Waluigi also hopes that if there ARE lingering effects, Smoking J has access to proper medical attention, though 'proper medical attention' is hard to find when reality has shattered into three pieces and everyone is trapped in hostile dimensions.

WAH.

name: Captain Syrup
title: The Pirate Queen of Rogueport
status: Active — Shelling everything in sight at Rogueport Bay
summary: Captain Syrup is the undisputed Pirate Queen of the seas, leader of the Black Sugar Pirates, and one of the few people whose greed might actually rival Wario's. She is currently engaged in a massive naval war in Rogueport Bay against the Iron Legion and the Mushroom Regency. Waluigi has a professional rivalry with Syrup. She thinks she's the best thief in the world. Waluigi *knows* he is.
description:
Waluigi respects Captain Syrup, though he would never admit it to her face. She runs a pirate empire with the kind of ruthless efficiency that Wario wishes he had. She doesn't bother with political ideologies or dimensional fractures. She sees a ship full of gold, she shoots cannons at it, she takes the gold. It is a wonderfully simple business model.

**The Battle of Rogueport**
Syrup and her fleet are currently the wildcard in the Coastal Provinces. The Iron Legion wants to blockade and tax the oceans. The Mushroom Regency wants to maintain order. Syrup just wants to sink both of them and loot the wreckage. 

When the Rakasha priest accidentally teleported the Toad scouts (Mystivl and Big R) directly onto a ship in Rogueport Bay, they arrived exactly as Captain Syrup yelled, 'Fire the cannons!' This is the quintessential Captain Syrup experience: arriving anywhere near her usually means you are about to explode.

**Assessment**
If the civil war continues to escalate, Syrup's naval superiority will become a massive factor. Whoever controls the sea controls the trade routes, and right now, Syrup is making sure nobody controls anything without paying her a toll in blood and cannonballs. Waluigi hopes to avoid Rogueport Bay until the smoke clears, but he fully intends to steal her ship someday just to see the look on her face. WAH.

name: Vivian Corvinarus
title: The Impostor Heir
race: Unknown — possibly Human, confirmed not a Toad, confirmed not blood-related to the Corvinarus family
status: Deceased — killed by Markop during interrogation aftermath, body burned
affiliation: Self-Interested / Shadow Estate (Infiltrator, not legitimate heir)
summary: Vivian Corvinarus was not a Corvinarus. Was not female. Was not whatever the dinner guests assumed. Vivian was an impostor who arrived at the Shadow Estate disguised as 'Vivinessa'—a thrall to the manor—and worked their way close to the heirs through deception, patience, and a wig. Their goal was sole inheritance: kill Orangus Cornelius, kill Kyrn Corvinarus, eliminate all other succession claimants, and become the sole ruler of an isolated dimensional pocket. They wielded death magic that BYPASSED the Shadowfell's suppression—a crimson disintegration beam that nearly killed Markop and required divine intervention to survive. They had been 'blighting' manor residents, including the Mazebounds in the hedge grove. They were defeated by Markop and Bowser, captured, interrogated, and killed. Waluigi finds Vivian fascinating in the way a poisonous insect is fascinating—beautiful adaptation, terrible purpose, best observed from a distance. Preferably after someone else has dealt with it. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Vivian Corvinarus with the acknowledgment that most of what Waluigi knows comes from a single interrogation conducted by Markop and Bowser after Vivian's capture. Interrogation testimony from a defeated enemy should be treated with appropriate skepticism—the captured lie to mislead, to buy time, to plant disinformation. But some of what Vivian said was corroborated by evidence, and the portrait that emerges is both impressive and deeply disturbing.

## The Deception — How Vivian Infiltrated

Vivian did not storm the Shadow Estate. Did not fight their way in. Did not use magic to breach the defenses.

Vivian APPLIED.

They arrived at the manor disguised as 'Vivinessa'—a thrall, the lowest position in the Onyx Hand's hierarchy. A servant. Nobody. The kind of person that centuries-old vampires notice only when their goblet is empty.

From that position, Vivian worked their way upward. Close to the staff. Close to the household. Close to the heirs. The Mazebound who provided intelligence during the interrogation described it simply: 'They arrived, disguised as a person named Vivinessa, a thrall to the manor, and they got close to the heir. And that's history.'

The wig was part of the disguise. When Markop checked it after Vivian's defeat, he found it was human hair—cut, glued to Vivian's actual hair with adhesive. Not magical transformation. Not illusion. Physical disguise. Prosthetics and performance.

Vivian maintained this deception long enough to become trusted. Long enough to attend dinners. Long enough to learn the manor's secrets. Long enough to begin implementing their actual plan.

Waluigi respects the DISCIPLINE this represents even while being horrified by the PURPOSE it served. Maintaining a false identity among vampires—beings who can smell blood, detect heartbeats, sense deception through supernatural means—requires either extraordinary acting skill or extraordinary countermeasures. Vivian apparently had both.

## The Blight — Vivian's Weapon

Vivian's method of control was not simple violence. It was BLIGHT.

Blighting—as Vivian described it during interrogation—was a process of corruption that gradually gave Vivian influence over the blighted individual. The Mazebounds in the hedge grove were blight victims. Former residents of the manor, transformed by Vivian's magic into grey-skinned, singing predators who served Vivian's territorial interests.

The musical theatre aspect of the Mazebounds—the choreographed songs, the jazz hands, the patter numbers about dividing and conquering—may have been a side effect of the blight process, or it may have been deliberate. Vivian seemed amused by their victims' behavior, which suggests either artistic intention or sociopathic entertainment.

'The Mazebounds were all blighted once,' Vivian told Markop during interrogation. 'Yet...' The trailing sentence implied more blighting was planned. The entire manor population was the target.

## The Death Beam — Magic That Broke the Rules

The Shadowfell suppresses magic. This is established fact. Archie's fire was completely extinguished upon arrival. Standard spellcasting becomes unreliable or impossible.

Vivian's magic was NOT suppressed.

'Did you know the Shadowfell suppresses magic?' Vivian said, smiling. 'But not THIS magic.'

The crimson beam of disintegration that followed was death magic of a type that operated OUTSIDE the Shadowfell's suppressive field. Whether this was because death magic is native to the Shadowfell, because Vivian had found a loophole in the dimensional mechanics, or because the magic came from a source that transcended planar suppression, Waluigi cannot determine.

What Waluigi CAN determine is the effect: the beam nearly killed Markop—the most durable, capable combatant in Disaster Inc. Only divine intervention saved him. Vivian's spell components were subsequently destroyed, preventing a repeat, but the existence of Shadowfell-compatible death magic raises alarming questions about what other weapons might function in suppressed dimensions.

## The Plan — Isolation and Control

Vivian's goals, as described during interrogation:

**Step One: Eliminate the heirs.** Orangus Cornelius was recovering from Green T's assault during the dinner. Vivian wanted him dead. Kyrn Corvinarus was next. Once both legitimate heirs were eliminated, Vivian—as the last surviving 'family member'—would inherit by default.

**Step Two: Eliminate witnesses.** The party was a complication. Vivian attacked Markop and Bowser not for personal reasons but because they were obstacles to succession. 'Three things changed since the dinner,' Vivian said. They declined to specify what those three things were.

**Step Three: Close the planar fractures.** Not to restore normality. To ISOLATE the Shadow Estate. Vivian intended to sever all connections between the estate and other planes, creating an enclosed dimensional pocket under their sole control.

**Step Four: Rule.** With the estate isolated and all opposition blighted or eliminated, Vivian would become the absolute ruler of a private dimension. No outside interference. No competing powers. Total control.

The ambition is breathtaking. The methodology—deception, corruption, assassination, dimensional manipulation—is terrifying. Vivian was not merely a murderer. They were an architect of WORLDS, building toward a reality shaped entirely by their will.

## The Interrogation — What Was Revealed

Markop and Bowser's interrogation of Vivian after capture produced several revelations:

**Not a Corvinarus.** Vivian was not blood-related to the family. The entire claim to inheritance was fabricated. The Mazebounds confirmed this: 'The person before you is not blood related to the Corvinarus family.'

**Not female.** Despite presenting as Vivinessa—a female thrall—Vivian was actually male. 'Oh, and they arrived to this—Vivian is a boy, actually,' the Mazebound noted. The entire gender presentation was part of the disguise.

**The wig.** Physical disguise, not magical. Hair cut from an unknown source, glued into place. When checked for magic, none was found. This suggests Vivian relied on mundane deception rather than magical illusion—possibly because illusion magic would be suppressed by the Shadowfell.

**Vivian was entertained.** Throughout the interrogation, Vivian displayed a crooked smile and theatrical manner. They recited lines from the Mazebounds' songs. They gave a 'kill' versus 'blight' distinction with evident pleasure. They were not frightened of their captors.

This suggests either supreme confidence in eventual escape, total indifference to death, or the personality of someone who views their own destruction as another performance.

## The Death — Markop's Decision

Markop stabbed Vivian in the chest during the interrogation's conclusion. The decision was not rage—Markop does not act from rage. It was assessment. Vivian was too dangerous to imprison, too resourceful to contain, and too willing to harm others to be released.

The body was subsequently burned. The ashes were scattered by wind when a guard attempted to transport them.

Whether Vivian is truly dead remains an open question in a dimension where death magic functions freely. Waluigi notes that in the Shadowfell, 'dead' is a more flexible concept than elsewhere.

## Marcus Ashfold — The Observer

After Vivian's death, the party encountered Marcus Ashfold—who introduced himself as Orangus Cornelius's military consultant. He claimed to have been watching the battle unfold and 'taking notes.' He mentioned keeping an eye on 'the three ey—' before cutting himself off and walking away.

What was he about to say? The three-eyed what? Archie's Third Eye connection? Something else entirely?

Waluigi notes the detail and files it for future investigation.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Vivian Corvinarus is either dead or pretending to be dead in a dimension where pretending to be dead is a viable survival strategy.

If dead: they were a remarkable infiltrator, a dangerous combatant, and an ambitious architect of private realities. Their death removes a significant threat from the Shadow Estate.

If alive: everything they revealed during interrogation may have been calculated disinformation, and the party is in more danger than they realize.

Waluigi hopes Vivian is dead. Waluigi does not have confidence in that hope.

The impostor who built an identity from scratch, infiltrated a vampire court through service, blighted an entire grove into musical servitude, and wielded death magic in a dimension that suppresses all other forms—that person does not seem like the type to die easily.

Waluigi advises extreme caution regarding any future claims that Vivian Corvinarus is gone for good. In the Shadowfell, death is a starting position, not a conclusion.

WAH.

name: Orangus Cornelius
title: The Defenestrated Lord
status: Active (Barely) — Shot with silver, tackled out a window, and deeply humiliated
summary: Orangus Cornelius was the senior vampire lord of the Shadow Estate and a figure of absolute authority. Then Green T shot him with a silver bullet from the children's table. Unfortunately, Cornelius survived. Instead of dying gracefully, he turned into a giant bat, got tackled through a window by Bowser, and watched his precious dimensional Anchor get shattered. Waluigi considers surviving this sequence of events physically impressive but socially fatal.
description:
Orangus Cornelius represented everything Waluigi finds irritating about aristocracy: the assumption of superiority, the elaborate social rituals designed to remind everyone of their place, the casual cruelty dressed up as tradition. He hosted dinner parties where guests were forced to vote on who would die. He seated guests at a CHILDREN'S TABLE as a deliberate insult. He maintained a court of thralls and servants and vampiric subordinates who existed to affirm his magnificence.

And then the children's table shot him.

Waluigi cannot stress enough how PERFECT this initial moment was. Orangus spent centuries cultivating an image of untouchable power. He probably thought he was the most dangerous thing in any room he entered. But as Waluigi recently learned from the survival accounts of Disaster Inc., a silver bullet to the chest was only the BEGINNING of Cornelius's terrible, horrible, no-good, very bad evening.

## The Dinner Party and the Shot

Orangus's dinner parties were exercises in vampire social dominance. The formal settings, the elaborate courses, the vote tradition—all of it designed to remind guests that they existed at Orangus's pleasure. He could kill anyone at any time. Archie had to cut off Usk's finger to prove loyalty in this environment. The entire evening was designed to break down the guests' sense of moral autonomy and replace it with submission to Orangus's will.

Green T disrupted this dynamic with a firearm and silver ammunition. Silver is anathema to vampires. It doesn't heal properly. It burns. It ruins the aesthetic. Orangus took a silver bullet from someone he had dismissed as a minor nuisance, proving once again that arrogance is a terminal disease.

## The Defenestration of Cornelius

Because vampires are dramatic, Cornelius did not simply fall over and die from the silver bullet. Instead, he dropped the aristocratic pretense and transformed into a giant bat monster. Waluigi finds this incredibly cliché, but it did escalate the situation rapidly.

This transformation prompted Bowser to do what Bowser does best: apply overwhelming physical force. Bowser tackled the giant bat-vampire lord straight through the dining room window and into the courtyard. Getting thrown out of a window in your own house is objectively the most embarrassing thing that can happen to a host. In the ensuing wrestling match, Bowser actually bit Cornelius's wing. A giant, fire-breathing turtle bit a giant, undead bat. The Shadowfell is a very weird place.

## The Shattered Anchor

The ultimate insult to Cornelius wasn't the bullet or the bite—it was the loss of his dimensional control. During the courtyard brawl, the 'Shadow Anchor'—a glowing purple crystal hidden inside a hollow statue—was exposed. Cornelius lunged to protect it, desperate to maintain the magical suppression of his domain.

Green T, firing from the shattered window above, shot the crystal. The Anchor exploded into dust, instantly returning color and fire magic to the Shadowfell. Cornelius failed to protect his own planar infrastructure in front of his entire surviving court.

## Current Status

Orangus Cornelius is ALIVE, much to Waluigi's disappointment. However, his authority is completely shattered. He has been shot with silver, beaten by a turtle, thrown through a window, and stripped of his magical planar dominance.

His weakness has thrown the Onyx Hand into chaos. Vivian, the hidden claimant to the Corvinarus Heir title, is currently wandering the estate's halls, openly admitting to Remi that he is simply waiting for Cornelius to succumb to his wounds so he can take over. When your rivals don't even bother assassinating you because they assume you're pathetic enough to expire on your own, your political career is officially over.

Waluigi expects Cornelius will seek violent, terrible revenge if he recovers. But for now, the 'untouchable' lord of the Shadowfell is just a wounded bat hiding in a Technicolor ruin. WAH.

name: Lady Aurelian Corvinarus
title: The Weaver of the Three Threads
status: Active — Plotting the endgame of the Manors
summary: Lady Aurelian continues to play 4D chess while everyone else is playing checkers. She has revealed that the party is currently trapped in the past—Year 722 of the Eternal Bloom. She requires Bone, Ash, Chalk, and Iron to repair a dimensional circle. She is also intimately connected to a horrific historical event called 'The Grafting.' Waluigi hates time travel, and he hates her riddles even more.
description:
Lady Aurelian is not just a polite host; she is the anchor of a timeline that is actively unraveling. Waluigi and the party discovered that the Feyward manor is currently existing in the year 722 of the local calendar, during the 'Prime Magic Month' when entropy is low. 

**The Grafting (Year 988)**
Through a combination of Usk's ghostly visions and Aurelian's own diary (which Toad Lee helpfully read aloud), the party learned about a horrific event known as 'The Grafting.' In the year 988, Orangus Cornelius (or another orange-robed Corvinarus) cut his own palm over a screaming dragon egg. The Iron Legion was present to observe the ritual, hoping to promise 'control' over whatever monstrosity hatched from the vine and scale. This event split the bloodline.

**The Circle Repair**
Aurelian is actively trying to construct or repair a magic circle in her master bedroom. She tasked Hjumpik with gathering the ritual components: Bone, Ash, Chalk, and Iron (which the goblins tried to harvest from Remi's dog). Aurelian cryptically noted that there are 'Three manors, three lords, three threads. Cut one, and the tapestry unravels.' She intends to sever the planes to save her own present, which would likely doom everyone in the other dimensions. 

Waluigi is keeping a very close eye on her. You never trust a woman who sleeps in a bed made of giant carnivorous flowers.

name: Azure (Rakasha)
title: The Intoxicated Mystic
status: Active — Rakasha faction member, situationally allied with the party but not owned by their disaster
affiliation: Rakasha Tribes / party-adjacent ally of Disaster Inc. (not a core member)
summary: Azure is a Rakasha spirit-walker who is currently operating under the influence of extreme Feywild theatrical magic. She is abnormally strong, prone to speaking in rhyming couplets, and can manifest giant glowing ghost-hands. She saved Toad Lee from a lethal fall and squished a goblin guard without noticing. Waluigi is slightly terrified of her.
description:
The Feywild affects everyone differently. It makes Waluigi paranoid. It makes Toad Lee violent. It makes Azure, the Rakasha, act like a heavily intoxicated theater kid with god-like strength.

**The Theater Hypnosis**
After watching a play in the Overgrown Library, Azure entered a state of 'bliss' that fundamentally altered her capabilities. When Hjumpik tried to quietly guide her away, she grabbed his arm and dragged him through the halls with a physical strength that Hjumpik—a seasoned warrior—could not resist. Toad Lee couldn't stop her either. She skipped through the manor, happily declaring they were having a sleepover.

**Spectral Capabilities**
Despite her compromised mental state, Azure is incredibly dangerous. During the skirmish in the servant's quarters, when Toad Lee was falling out a window, Azure's hand turned blue and manifested a massive, mystic ghost-hand that reached out and pulled the Toad back inside. She then casually walked over an unconscious goblin (*squish*), grabbed Remi's mechanical dog, and walked out without breaking stride. 

Azure also confirmed the party's worst fears through a rhyming song: they are indeed trapped in the past (*'The dates don’t match, the ink is wet / We’re in a time we haven’t happened yet!'*). Waluigi appreciates the information, but wishes she would deliver it without singing. WAH.

name: Wario
title: The Explosive Accountant
status: Active — inside the Shadow Estate escape sequence, seeking the Mirror of True Reflection after Scarecrow is killed and reserving loot rights on Scarecrow’s body
summary:
Wario has breached the Feywild, and he brought explosives. He attempted to blow up a giant insect with a wrapped present just to steal its silver, survived a multi-story fall without blinking, and is aggressively enforcing a ledger of debts. Waluigi officially and legally disputes the 14,783 gold pieces Wario claims Waluigi owes him. That interest rate is extortion!

Wario is no longer merely “somewhere in the Feywild counting his money” for this file’s purposes. Current Shadow Estate reports place him in the mirror recovery sequence: picking a lock silently, smelling money with professional skill, attempting to swipe the newly restored Mirror of True Reflection, being stopped by Markop, and negotiating the kind of bargain only Wario would consider fair: he helps with remaining business and Scarecrow, then he gets the mirror afterward and loot rights on Scarecrow’s body.
description:
Waluigi has known Wario for longer than Waluigi cares to calculate. Their partnership began in the competitive sports circuit, expanded into business ventures, and has survived crises that would have shattered less durable relationships. Wario is not an easy person to work with—he is loud, he is demanding, he prioritizes profit over everything, and he genuinely cannot understand why anyone would do anything for free. But he is RELIABLE in his unreliability. You always know what Wario wants.

Or so Waluigi THOUGHT.

Then Wario faked his own death WITHOUT TELLING WALUIGI.

## The Fake Death

On Efferd 25th, 1040 BF—ONE DAY before the Swiftsoul explosion that got Archie framed for murder—Wario held his own funeral. The event was heavily guarded by Iron Fists Guild members. The casket was closed. Two clockwork automata resembling Wario mingled with mourners.

The casket, according to informants who actually CHECKED, contained weighted sacks. NOT A BODY. Meanwhile, Wario himself was reportedly seen gambling at a Dockside den DURING THE FUNERAL SERVICE.

Waluigi was not informed of this plan. Waluigi attended the funeral believing his business partner was DEAD. Waluigi may have experienced EMOTIONS at this funeral. Waluigi is EXTREMELY annoyed that those emotions were wasted on an ELABORATE HOAX.

## What Was Wario Planning?

Piecing together evidence from the Swiftsoul case file, Waluigi has developed theories about what Wario was doing:

The Iron Fists Guild communique mentions 'Wario's folly created necessary opportunity for adjustment.' This suggests Wario did SOMETHING that forced the Guild's hand—possibly a failed double-cross related to Dragon Mountain and the events that led to Edgeshade's destruction.

Archie's encoded ledger contains an entry for 'W - Emergency Extraction Fund (Contingency Sigma).' This suggests Archie was holding money for Wario's emergency escape—which implies Wario KNEW he would need to disappear.

The volatile cargo on the Swift Quill blimp was destined for Edgeshade. Edgeshade is DESTROYED. Why would anyone ship volatile alchemical reagents to a destroyed town unless the shipment was cover for something else, or unless the sender didn't know about the destruction?

A greasy wrench matching Wario's tools was found at the Swiftsoul blast site. Clockwork gears and a crushed clockwork bird were found along the escape route. These items are consistent with Wario's technology.

Waluigi's theory: Wario's scheme with the Iron Fists went wrong. The Guild decided to eliminate him, or he decided to disappear preemptively, and the 'funeral' was cover for his vanishing act. The Swiftsoul explosion was either part of the Guild's cleanup operation or an unintended consequence of volatile cargo, and Archie—who had worked with Wario through Rakka—was the convenient fall guy.

Wario is ALIVE. Wario is HIDING. And Wario has left a MESS that other people are paying for.

## Business Philosophy

Wario's approach to business is simple: find valuable things, acquire valuable things, sell valuable things (or keep them, if keeping is more profitable than selling). This approach lacks nuance, ethics, or concern for consequences, but it WORKS. Wario's Enterprise has survived crises that destroyed more 'legitimate' organizations because Wario doesn't depend on reputation, ideology, or political positioning. He depends on having things other people want.

The Enterprise's current activities include treasure acquisition, debt collection, mercenary contracting, and 'opportunity logistics'—which is Wario's term for grabbing valuable items during chaotic situations when nobody's paying attention. The Vigilance Crisis has been EXCELLENT for opportunity logistics. Chaos creates opportunities. Opportunities create profit. Profit creates happiness (for Wario).

Of course, THIS time the chaos apparently includes faking his death, getting involved with dangerous Guild operations, and letting his associates take the blame for explosions. Waluigi will be having WORDS with Wario about this.

## The Edgeshade Connection

Wario and Waluigi were both present when dragons destroyed Edgeshade. The official story is that the dragons were provoked by... unspecified actions. Waluigi maintains that the dragons made their OWN choices and cannot be BLAMED on anyone who may or may not have interacted with eggs, treasure hoards, or territorial boundaries.

However, the case file evidence suggests deeper connections. Wario was apparently working with the Iron Fists Guild on something related to Edgeshade, Dragon Mountain, or both. The volatile cargo destined for the destroyed town implies ongoing operations even after the destruction. And the Guild's communique explicitly mentions 'Wario's folly' as creating 'necessary opportunity.'

Wario's schemes have always been ambitious. This time, they may have intersected with forces—dragons, guilds, criminal syndicates—that even Wario cannot outmaneuver through sheer audacity.

## Physical Capabilities

Wario is not subtle. He is not graceful. He is not, by any conventional measure, aesthetically pleasing. But he is DURABLE in ways that defy explanation. Waluigi has seen Wario survive falls, explosions, impacts, and digestive challenges that should have killed any normal person. Wario's body seems to reject damage through sheer stubbornness, as if the universe has tried to kill him so many times that it's given up.

This durability probably explains how Wario survived whatever actually happened before his 'death.' The man does not die easily. The man does not die AT ALL, apparently, even when he holds a funeral for himself.

## Relationship with Waluigi

Wario is the closest thing Waluigi has to family in a practical sense. Not because they share blood—Waluigi does not actually know if he and Wario are related—but because they share UNDERSTANDING. Wario doesn't expect Waluigi to be something he's not. Wario accepts Waluigi's ambitions, tolerates his grievances, and partners with him as an equal (or as close to equal as Wario gets with anyone).

The partnership is not sentimental. Wario would sell Waluigi out for enough money—Waluigi knows this and has accepted it. But the price would have to be VERY high, because Waluigi is valuable to the Enterprise and Wario doesn't throw away valuable assets. This mutual understanding of each other's limits is, in its own way, more reliable than friendship.

That said, FAKING YOUR DEATH WITHOUT TELLING YOUR BUSINESS PARTNER is a VIOLATION of that understanding. Waluigi experienced GRIEF. Waluigi attended a FUNERAL. Waluigi may have shed a SINGLE DIGNIFIED TEAR, which he will DENY if asked. And the whole time, Wario was GAMBLING in a DOCKSIDE DEN.

Waluigi is going to find Wario. Waluigi is going to demand explanations. And Waluigi is going to charge Wario for emotional damages at a SUBSTANTIAL rate.

## Current Status

Wario's current location is unknown. He successfully faked his death and disappeared, which means he could be anywhere—hiding from the Iron Fists, running new schemes, counting his coins in some remote hideout, or possibly already involved in the next disaster waiting to happen.

Knowing Wario, he's making money somewhere. The crisis will eventually produce a profitable angle, and Wario will find it. When the party reunites—and they WILL reunite—Wario will probably show up with pockets full of coins and a complete lack of understanding about why everyone is angry with him.

Waluigi looks forward to this conversation. It will be LOUD. Wario does not care about dimensional instability, fey politics, or the collapse of reality. Wario cares about his Ledger. 

**The Ledger of Debts**
Wario produced his accounting book during a meeting with Hjumpik and Toad Lee, and Waluigi's blood pressure spikes just reading the transcript. Wario claims Bowser owes him 50,000 GP for 'storage fees' (Wario stole the treasure, he isn't storing it!). He is charging Remi 75 GP for a healing potion. Most offensively, he claims Waluigi owes him 14,783 gold pieces for 'partnership expenses' dating back to 1015 BF, compounded at 15% interest. Waluigi absolutely refuses to pay this. The garlic budget alone accounts for half of that deficit!

**Combat and Inventory**
Wario's approach to Feywild combat is glorious. He wears custom brass knuckles stamped with 'W's, shoulder-bashes doors, and uses a broken coin-press as a bludgeoning tool. During the Solarium incident, he tried to feed a ticking time-bomb (wrapped with a lovely bow) to a giant Bramblefly. When Hjumpik accidentally detonated it early, Wario fell through the floor, landed in a pile of treasure, and instantly started pocketing silver while his overalls were still smoking.

Wario also possesses several bottles of 268-year-old Vampire Wine looted from the Shadow Estate. The wine heals wounds, grants darkvision, and turns your blood toxic to vampires. Wario drinks it like grape juice and sells it for 750 GP a bottle. The man is an economic titan.

## Recent Update — The Mirror Bargain

Wario’s legal position is that he never said the party could keep the mirror; he only said he could have it. Waluigi has reviewed this argument and finds it spiritually Wario-shaped. The current field arrangement is that Green T holds the Mirror of True Reflection while Wario cooperates until Scarecrow is dead. Waluigi recommends watching the bag of holding.

name: Princess Peach
title: The Fallen Monarch
status: Deceased — assassinated under circumstances that remain disputed
summary: Princess Peach is dead. The circumstances of her assassination remain unresolved, fueling the Peach Loyalists' crusade and shaping the political landscape of the entire Mushroom Kingdom. Waluigi knew Peach through competitive sports events, and he can say with certainty that the woman Captain Toadette is avenging bears no resemblance to the woman Waluigi actually met. The real Peach was kind, gracious, and would have been horrified by what is being done in her name.
description:
Waluigi competed against Princess Peach numerous times—tennis tournaments, go-kart races, party game events. In those contexts, Peach was a formidable competitor with excellent technique and, more importantly, genuine sportsmanship. She won with grace. She lost with grace. She treated opponents as equals deserving of respect, which is more than Waluigi can say for CERTAIN PLUMBER BROTHERS who shall remain named Mario and Luigi.

Waluigi did not know Peach WELL. They were competitors, not friends. But he knew her well enough to recognize that the version of Peach the Loyalists have constructed—a princess who would approve of executing prisoners, who would demand total war, who would consider atrocities acceptable costs—does not match the person he met.

## The Assassination

The details of Peach's assassination remain partially obscured. Intelligence gathered by various factions—including Loyalist scouts like Embercap and Mistveil—has revealed fragments: involvement of powerful figures, secrets hidden in Peach's private chambers, connections to political networks that operated in shadows. But the full picture remains incomplete.

This incompleteness is part of why the Loyalists are so dangerous. They don't KNOW who killed Peach or why. They have suspicions, leads, fragments of evidence. The uncertainty fuels their rage. Anyone COULD be responsible. Everyone is suspect until proven otherwise. And 'proven otherwise' requires a level of evidence that the Loyalists can conveniently never quite accept.

## Legacy

Peach's legacy has been weaponized by people who probably never knew her. Captain Toadette wages total war in Peach's name. The Loyalists execute prisoners for Peach's cause. A movement dedicated to a dead princess has become one of the most brutal factions in the Mushroom Kingdom.

Waluigi finds this deeply tragic. Not because he was close to Peach—he wasn't—but because he understands what it means to have your image used for purposes you would never have approved. Peach cannot object to what's being done in her name. She's dead. Her memory belongs to whoever shouts loudest, and the people shouting loudest are people with swords.

If Peach's ghost exists—if she's watching what's happening from some spiritual plane—Waluigi imagines she's HORRIFIED. The princess who treated tennis opponents with respect would not have wanted prisoners executed in her honor. The princess who competed fairly would not have wanted total war conducted under her banner.

But ghosts don't get votes. Living people with armies do. And the living people with armies have decided that Princess Peach's memory demands blood.

Waluigi hopes someone eventually uncovers the truth of Peach's assassination. Not because justice matters—Waluigi is cynical about justice—but because maybe, MAYBE, the truth would give the Loyalists something to focus on besides atrocities. Maybe knowing WHO killed Peach would let them direct their rage somewhere specific instead of spraying it at everyone.

Maybe.

Waluigi is not optimistic. But he hopes.

WAH.

name: Fawful
title: The Cackling Conqueror
status: Active — losing territory but still dangerous
summary: Fawful is a cackling megalomaniac who speaks in the third person, rants about mustard, and has somehow conquered significant portions of the Mushroom Kingdom through a combination of mechanical armies, technological superiority, and sheer overwhelming ENERGY. Waluigi finds him deeply irritating for reasons he cannot fully articulate. Possibly because Waluigi ALSO occasionally speaks in the third person but does it with STYLE, whereas Fawful does it while screaming about condiments.
description:
Fawful defies easy categorization. He is a villain, certainly—he conquers territory, commands armies, and threatens the established order. But he is also ABSURD in ways that make taking him seriously difficult. His speech patterns are incomprehensible. His plans are grandiose to the point of parody. His relationship with sanity is, at best, long-distance.

And yet. He has an army. He holds territory. He has technological capabilities that exceed most factions'. The absurdity does not make him less dangerous—it makes him UNPREDICTABLE, which is its own kind of dangerous.

## Military Position

Fawful's forces held significant Mushroom Kingdom territory at the start of the crisis, including the fortified bastion of Bramblehaven. His occupation was characterized by mechanical efficiency—automated defenses, construct patrols, and garrison troops who operated under Fawful's unique command style.

The Fall of Bramblehaven was the first major crack in Fawful's position. The Peach Loyalists broke his garrison through overwhelming force and total commitment, demonstrating that Fawful's mechanical armies could be beaten by sufficiently determined organic opposition. Subsequent territorial losses have forced Fawful to consolidate, abandoning smaller holdings to reinforce core positions.

Fawful's empire is shrinking. But it is not yet broken. Underestimating Fawful because he speaks strangely would be a mistake. He has pulled dramatic reversals before—superweapons, unexpected alliances, technological innovations that nobody anticipated. The cackling may be annoying, but the brain behind it is genuinely clever.

## Personal Interaction

Waluigi has encountered Fawful peripherally and found the experience deeply unpleasant. Not because Fawful is threatening in person—though he is—but because COMMUNICATION with Fawful is like trying to read a book that's being shouted at you by someone who considers coherent sentences a sign of weakness.

Fawful speaks in metaphors that reference foods. He talks about himself in third person. He cackles at irregular intervals. He uses the word 'fury' more frequently than anyone should. A simple conversation becomes an exercise in translation, where you try to figure out what Fawful actually MEANS while he screams about the mustard of your doom.

Waluigi's patience for this is LIMITED. Waluigi values clear communication—when Waluigi says something, he means it. When Fawful says something, it requires a decoder ring and possibly a food dictionary.

## Assessment

Fawful remains a significant player in Mushroom Kingdom politics despite his territorial losses. His technological base is largely intact. His mechanical production capabilities continue. His personal cunning—hidden behind the absurdist presentation—should not be underestimated.

Waluigi expects Fawful to produce some dramatic countermove eventually. A superweapon. A dimensional portal. A mechanical army upgrade. Something that nobody sees coming because they're too busy laughing at his speech patterns. Fawful has a history of such reversals.

Until that reversal comes, Fawful is on the defensive. But defensive Fawful is not defeated Fawful. The cackling continues. The planning continues. The mustard of doom, whatever that means, presumably continues as well.

WAH.

name: Usk
title: The One Who Lost a Finger
