status: Active — missing one finger, trust severely damaged
summary: Usk is the person whose finger Archie Miser cut off to prove loyalty to the vampire lords during the Shadow Estate dinner party. Waluigi was not present for this event but has thought about it extensively. Usk was an ally. Archie cut off his finger. The tactical necessity does not change the fundamental betrayal of trust that moment represented. Waluigi does not know how Usk and Archie's relationship recovers from this, if it recovers at all.
description:
Waluigi did not know Usk well before the Shadow Estate dinner. Usk was part of the group that ended up in the Shadowfell, one of the allies navigating vampire politics alongside Archie and Bowser. By all accounts, Usk was competent, reliable, and trusted by the people around him.

Then Archie cut off his finger.

## The Incident

The vampires demanded proof of Archie's loyalty to their court. Archie was operating under his Darman Knightly cover, playing the role of a guest who might be useful to the Onyx Hand's interests. The cover was keeping him alive. But covers require maintenance, and the vampires wanted blood.

Archie was told to cut off Usk's finger. Archie did it.

Waluigi has thought about this moment more than he probably should. The tactical calculus is clear: Archie needed to maintain his cover, the cover required demonstrating loyalty, demonstrating loyalty required visible sacrifice, and Usk's finger was available. From a pure survival perspective, Archie made the 'correct' choice.

But tactical correctness is not the same as moral correctness. You can justify an action and still have that action be WRONG. You can understand why someone did something and still hold them accountable for doing it. Archie cut off an ally's finger to impress vampires. The finger is gone. Usk carries that absence forever.

## The Trust Problem

Waluigi thinks about what it must feel like to be Usk. To be surrounded by enemies in a dark dimension. To look at your allies as the only people you can rely on. And then to have one of those allies—someone you trusted, someone you fought alongside—take a blade and remove a piece of your body to prove something to monsters.

How do you trust that person again? How do you fight alongside them knowing what they're capable of? Every time Archie faces a difficult choice, Usk now knows that Archie will sacrifice allies if the tactical situation demands it. That knowledge changes EVERYTHING about how you relate to someone.

Waluigi has been betrayed before. Not as dramatically as losing a finger, but he understands the feeling of having someone you trusted prove that their trust had limits. It reshapes how you see them. You can forgive—maybe—but you can't forget. The knowledge lives in you: this person did this thing. This person could do it again.

## Assessment

Waluigi does not know Usk's current emotional state or his relationship with Archie. The party is scattered across dimensions, and Waluigi is not in the Shadowfell to observe how Usk and Archie are navigating their broken trust.

Waluigi hopes Usk survives. Waluigi hopes Usk finds a way to process what happened without it consuming him. Waluigi hopes, against hope, that Usk and Archie can rebuild something functional—not because Archie deserves forgiveness, but because the party needs to work together to survive and escape.

But Waluigi also hopes Usk never forgets what Archie did. Some things should be remembered. Some things should inform future decisions. Archie cut off a friend's finger. That is who Archie is, at least sometimes, under pressure, when survival is on the line.

Remember that.

WAH.

name: Roger
title: The Poisoner
status: Active — possesses poisoned daggers of unusual potency
summary: Roger is the person whose poisoned dagger caused Earl Grey to literally explode during the Syndicate Showdown. The poison's interaction with Earl Grey's physiology was completely unexpected and remains unexplained. Roger has carried poisoned weapons throughout the campaign, which makes him valuable in combat and EXTREMELY concerning in any situation where accidental poisoning is a possibility. Waluigi stands at least ten feet away from Roger at all times.
description:
Roger is one of those allies who Waluigi appreciates in combat and avoids in casual situations. His weapons are poisoned. His daggers are coated with substances that cause effects ranging from paralysis to—as Earl Grey dramatically demonstrated—EXPLOSIVE biological reactions. Having Roger on your side in a fight is excellent. Being near Roger when he's eating dinner is less excellent, because Waluigi does not know if Roger's utensils are also poisoned and Waluigi would prefer not to find out.

## Combat Effectiveness

Roger's primary contribution to any engagement is the poisoned element of his attacks. A normal dagger wound requires medical attention. A Roger-dagger wound requires medical attention, antidotes, prayers, and possibly a bomb disposal team depending on what the poison does to your particular biology.

During the Syndicate Showdown, Roger landed a strike on Earl Grey that should have caused conventional poison effects—paralysis, unconsciousness, eventual death. Instead, Earl Grey EXPLODED. The poison interacted with something in Earl Grey's physiology and triggered a detonation that scattered items and biological matter across the marketplace.

Nobody has ever explained this. Roger's poison should not cause explosions. Earl Grey's physiology should not have been explosive. Something happened at the intersection of those two factors that defied all expectations. Waluigi's favorite hat was caught in the blast radius, which Waluigi considers a personal offense even though Roger presumably did not intend to detonate anyone.

## The Uncertainty Factor

The Earl Grey explosion raises uncomfortable questions about Roger's arsenal. If his poison can cause explosions under the right circumstances, what ELSE can it do? What other unexpected biological interactions are possible? If Roger stabs a vampire, will the vampire explode? If he stabs a fey creature, will it turn into something worse?

Waluigi does not know the answers. Waluigi suspects Roger doesn't know either. The poisons work—they definitely work—but their full effects may not be predictable across all possible targets. This makes Roger a wildcard in any engagement. Valuable, yes. But unpredictable in ways that could produce unexpected outcomes.

## Assessment

Roger is an effective combatant whose methods carry inherent uncertainty. Waluigi appreciates his contributions while maintaining a healthy distance from his weapons. The Earl Grey incident suggests that even Roger doesn't fully understand what his poisons might do to any given target.

Waluigi hopes Roger's poisons continue to work in the party's favor. Waluigi ALSO hopes that if Roger ever stabs Waluigi accidentally, the poison causes normal paralysis rather than explosive decompression. Waluigi would prefer to die in a dignified manner, not as a purple fountain in a marketplace.

WAH.

name: Mossy
title: The Stolen Construct
status: Active — last seen during the Spider Grove battle, damaged but functional
summary: Mossy is a Mages' Guild construct that was 'liberated' (stolen) during earlier events and has since served as a combat asset for Disaster Inc. Mossy does not speak, does not tire, does not panic, and bites things when pointed at them. Waluigi finds these qualities admirable. If more allies were like Mossy—reliable, uncomplaining, and willing to clamp mechanical jaws onto giant spider legs—Waluigi's life would be significantly easier.
description:
Mossy's origin is technically criminal. The construct belonged to the Mages' Guild, was acquired through methods that the Guild would describe as 'theft' and that Disaster Inc. would describe as 'opportunistic resource reallocation,' and has since been employed in operations that the Guild would probably object to if they knew about them.

Waluigi does not feel guilty about this. The Mages' Guild has MANY constructs. They can spare one. And Mossy has proven far more useful in active field operations than it ever would have been sitting in a Guild facility being used for research or whatever constructs normally do.

## Combat Performance

Mossy participated in the Battle of the Spider Grove alongside Waluigi and other party members. The construct provided reliable support throughout the engagement—no fear, no hesitation, no complaints about the webbing or the darkness or the dog-sized spiders trying to flank the group.

During the final phase, Mossy clamped its mechanical jaws onto one of the Arachnid Matriarch's rear legs and HELD ON. This was not a decisive attack, but it was a PERSISTENT one. While Markop grappled, while Waluigi fired arcane rays, while Salem's crossbow bolt pierced eyes, Mossy maintained pressure on the limb with the mindless determination that only a construct can muster.

The combined assault—from all sources, including Mossy—destabilized the Matriarch enough for the Oracle's banishment circle to work. Mossy contributed to that victory. Mossy deserves recognition for that contribution, even if Mossy cannot actually appreciate recognition because Mossy is a construct without apparent emotional processing.

## Construct Qualities

Waluigi appreciates several things about working with Mossy:

- Mossy does not argue about strategy
- Mossy does not require motivation or morale management
- Mossy does not get tired during extended operations
- Mossy does not panic when surrounded by giant spiders
- Mossy follows instructions with mechanical reliability
- Mossy bites things until told to stop

These qualities make Mossy an ideal ally for dangerous situations. Human allies have needs, opinions, emotions, and breaking points. Mossy has instructions and the physical capability to execute them. This simplicity is refreshing after dealing with fairy courts, vampire politics, and the general emotional chaos of Disaster Inc.

## Current Status

Waluigi does not know Mossy's current status. The construct was damaged during the Spider Grove battle but remained functional. The Planar Fracture presumably scattered Mossy along with everyone else, though constructs may interact with dimensional boundaries differently than organic beings.

If Mossy ended up in the Feywild with Waluigi, Waluigi would appreciate the company. Mossy would not be affected by fey social rules. Mossy would not accidentally create obligations by saying the wrong thing. Mossy would just be there, reliable and mechanical and uncomplicated.

Waluigi hopes Mossy survived and remains operational. Good constructs are hard to find, and Mossy has proven itself good.

WAH.

name: Toadburt
title: From Leashed Agent to Indentured Archivist
status: Active — real injured Toadburt confirmed alive at the Shadow Estate portal circle with Tanukiburt and Mystic Morel
affiliation: Formerly Iron Legion (coerced), currently Shadow Estate Archives (indentured)
summary:
Toadburt's story is a masterclass in trading one cage for another. The Iron Legion strapped an entropy ring on him and sent him into the Feywild as a coerced operative. Now the ring is off, but Toadburt isn't free—he's working for the Shadow Estate's Archivist in exchange for gradual healing, recovering from his injuries over two-week intervals while organizing books in a vampire library. Waluigi recognizes this pattern: someone too damaged to refuse help, accepting terms from whoever offers it, trading independence for survival. It's not slavery. It's not freedom. It's the grey area in between that nobody likes to name.

The Toadburt question has changed from unresolved suspicion to immediate rescue problem. Remi’s exterior scouting confirmed an injured real Toadburt gathered at the master-bedroom portal circle with Tanukiburt and Mystic Morel while the rug was being covered and uncovered. This means Toadburt is alive, not free, and positioned at the exact route the party needs to use.
description:
Waluigi has been tracking Toadburt's situation because Toadburt represents something that makes Waluigi ANGRY: a person who keeps getting used by institutions bigger than them.

## The Iron Legion Leash

After the Planar Fracture shattered reality around Raventree Manor, the Iron Legion seized the physical anchor point—the only stable connection between the three planar fragments. Then they grabbed Toadburt.

They fitted him with an entropy ring. Waluigi has described entropy rings elsewhere and will summarize: they are OBEDIENCE COLLARS. Magical devices that ensure compliance through the threat of very bad things happening to the wearer. The Iron Legion used Toadburt as a coerced agent, sending him into the Feywild to gather intelligence and pursue Legion objectives.

Toadburt didn't volunteer for this. Toadburt was SELECTED because he was available, controllable, and expendable. The Legion didn't need him specifically—they needed a body with a ring on it, and Toadburt was the body they had.

Waluigi has strong feelings about institutions that treat people as interchangeable components. Waluigi has BEEN treated as interchangeable. The difference is that Waluigi can fight back. Toadburt, ringed and coerced, could not.

## The Ring Comes Off

Somewhere in the Shadow Estate, Toadburt's entropy ring was removed. Remi noticed its absence during an encounter in the library—Toadburt was speaking with Pierce Anamatar, and the ring was simply GONE.

Waluigi doesn't know who removed it or why. Possible explanations:

The Archivist removed it as a condition of employment. Can't have Iron Legion tracking devices on your staff.

The ring malfunctioned in the Shadowfell's entropic environment. Ironic if an ENTROPY ring was destroyed by ENTROPY.

Toadburt found a way to remove it himself. Unlikely given the devices' design, but not impossible for someone desperate enough.

Someone in the Shadow Estate removed it to sever Iron Legion influence within the estate. Political housecleaning.

Regardless of how, the result is clear: Toadburt is no longer the Iron Legion's puppet. The leash is cut.

## The New Arrangement

But Toadburt isn't free. He's traded one form of control for another.

The Archivist has offered Toadburt a healing arrangement: gradual recovery from his injuries over two-week intervals. In exchange, Toadburt works within the Shadow Estate's archives. The healing is slow. The work is presumably constant. The arrangement has no defined endpoint that Waluigi is aware of.

Remi overheard part of the conversation between Toadburt and the Archivist. The Archivist explained the healing timeline as though it were reasonable—slow but steady, recovery through service. The framing was HELPFUL. The reality is indentured labor.

Waluigi has seen this before. Not in vampire estates—in REGULAR life. People too injured or desperate to refuse help, accepting terms from whoever extends a hand, gradually discovering that the hand expects PAYMENT and the payment never ends. The entropy ring was crude. The Archivist's arrangement is ELEGANT. Both achieve the same result: Toadburt serves someone else's interests because the alternative is worse.

## What Toadburt Knows

Toadburt spent time in the Feywild under Legion orders. He spent time in the Shadow Estate under the Archivist's arrangement. He has been INSIDE two of the three fractured dimensions. The intelligence he carries—about both the Feywild's conditions and the Shadow Estate's operations—is potentially significant.

The question is whether anyone has ASKED him. Toadburt has been treated as a tool by every faction that's handled him. Tools don't get asked for opinions. They get pointed at objectives and activated.

Waluigi thinks someone should sit down with Toadburt and actually LISTEN to what he's seen. Not debrief him—LISTEN. There's a difference. One treats the person as an intelligence asset. The other treats them as a person.

Waluigi has experience being treated as both. The second one is better.

## Assessment

Toadburt's trajectory is a miniature version of what's happening to everyone caught between larger factions. The Iron Legion used him. The Shadow Estate uses him. Neither asked what HE wanted. Neither offered genuine freedom as an option.

The entropy ring is off. That's progress. But progress from 'enslaved' to 'indentured' is a shorter distance than it should be.

Waluigi hopes Toadburt eventually reaches actual freedom. Waluigi suspects 'eventually' is doing a lot of heavy lifting in that sentence.

WAH.

## Recent Update — Confirmed at the Portal Circle

During The Mirror, the Roof, and the Fall, Remi saw Tanukiburt, the real injured Toadburt, and Mystic Morel in the master bedroom around the portal circle. This updates Toadburt’s status from “working under slow-healing arrangement” to “confirmed alive and in immediate danger/hostile custody at the exit point.” Waluigi marks this as a rescue flag.

name: The Rakasha
title: The People Beyond the Eastern Forests
status: Active — tribal confederation led by Chief Thornpaw
summary: The Rakasha are one of the older peoples in the regions surrounding the Mushroom Kingdom—a confederation of tribes inhabiting territories to the east and south. They are warriors, spirit-walkers, and keepers of dimensional traditions that predate the Mages' Guild by centuries. The Mushroom Kingdom's court conservatives viewed them with suspicion; the relationship between the two peoples has been complicated at best. Chief Thornpaw's revelation of his relationship with Princess Peach has reframed the Rakasha's position in the assassination narrative—from marginalized outsiders to central players in a conspiracy that may have been motivated partly by preventing a half-Rakasha heir from taking the throne. Their spirit-walker capabilities make them uniquely valuable in the current planar crisis. Their long memory makes them dangerous to those who would prefer history stay buried. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Rakasha as a people because understanding them is essential to understanding Chief Thornpaw, the assassination conspiracy theories, and the current dimensional crisis. Waluigi's knowledge is incomplete—the Rakasha are not inclined to share their traditions with outsiders—but Waluigi has gathered what information is available.

## Physical Characteristics — Not a Monolith

The Rakasha are often described as 'lion-like' or 'feline' in appearance. This description is... inadequate.

Waluigi has encountered Rakasha who fit the feline description—leonine features, manes, predatory grace. But Waluigi has also encountered Rakasha who appear more humanoid, more vulpine, more... other. The Rakasha are not a single physical type. They are a PEOPLE, and peoples contain variation.

What Rakasha share is not appearance but TRADITION. Their tribes are bound by shared spiritual practices, shared history, shared enemies. A Rakasha who looks nothing like another Rakasha is still Rakasha because they participate in Rakasha life.

Waluigi appreciates this. Waluigi knows what it is to be judged by appearance rather than substance. The Rakasha judge by participation and contribution. This is CORRECT.

## Territory and Organization

Rakasha territories lie east and south of the Mushroom Kingdom—forested lands, mountain ranges, places where the Kingdom's roads do not reach. These territories are not unified under a single government but organized as a tribal confederation. Each tribe maintains internal autonomy while participating in confederation decisions that affect all Rakasha.

Chief Thornpaw leads this confederation—a position he has held for approximately eighty-five years, which is remarkable by human standards but may be normal for Rakasha. Waluigi does not have reliable information about Rakasha lifespans. If they live significantly longer than humans, Thornpaw's tenure is less surprising. If they do not, his continued leadership suggests either exceptional capability or concerning centralization of power.

The confederation structure means Thornpaw does not rule by decree. He leads by consensus. Major decisions require tribal agreement. This makes the Rakasha slower to act than centralized powers but more stable once action is taken.

## Spirit-Walkers — Dimensional Capability

The most significant Rakasha capability for current purposes is their tradition of spirit-walking.

Spirit-walkers are individuals trained in practices that allow them to traverse dimensional boundaries, perceive across planar divides, and communicate through means that bypass physical limitations. These capabilities are spiritual rather than arcane—they do not require the spellcasting infrastructure the Mages' Guild uses.

This distinction matters. The Mages' Guild has spent centuries establishing itself as the authority on magical matters. The Rakasha spirit-walkers represent an alternative tradition—one the Guild cannot control, cannot regulate, cannot claim jurisdiction over. This made the Rakasha threatening to Guild interests long before the assassination.

In the current crisis, spirit-walker capabilities are increasingly valuable. The Planar Fracture has created dimensional instability that conventional magic struggles to address. Spirit-walkers, who have been navigating dimensional boundaries for generations, may have solutions that the Guild cannot provide.

Ryan of Disaster Inc. was taken in by a Rakasha spirit-walker after jumping from the Vigilance. This suggests the spirit-walkers are monitoring current events and choosing to intervene selectively. What they are preparing for—and whose interests they serve—remains unclear.

## Historical Relationship with the Mushroom Kingdom

The Rakasha's relationship with the Mushroom Kingdom has been... fraught.

Early records describe trade relationships and occasional conflicts—typical border-state dynamics. Rakasha goods moved through Kingdom markets. Kingdom travelers passed through Rakasha territories. The relationship was not warm but was functional.

As the Kingdom centralized under the monarchy, attitudes shifted. The Mages' Guild—which rose to prominence during the same period—viewed Rakasha spiritual practices with suspicion. Spirit-walking was dimensional magic conducted without Guild oversight. This was either threatening or heretical depending on which Guild faction you asked.

The court conservatives—the nobility who surrounded and advised the monarch—developed their own antipathy toward the Rakasha. Cultural differences were framed as barbarism. Religious differences were framed as deviance. The Rakasha became convenient Others against whom Kingdom identity could be defined.

By the time of Princess Peach's reign, inter-marriage between Kingdom citizens and Rakasha was technically legal but socially forbidden for anyone of noble rank. A ROYAL relationship with a Rakasha was unthinkable—the ultimate transgression against court conservative values.

This is the context in which Thornpaw and Peach allegedly fell in love. Every meeting was defiance. Every intimacy was rebellion. And the child they allegedly produced was either hope for a transformed future or nightmare fuel for everyone who preferred the old order.

## The Assassination and Its Aftermath

If the Loyalist narrative is accurate, the Rakasha were central victims of the assassination conspiracy.

The conspiracy's motive—preventing a half-Rakasha heir from taking the throne—made the Rakasha the implicit enemy. Their chief's relationship with the Princess was the 'problem' that murder was meant to solve. Their potential integration into Kingdom power structures was the future that death was meant to prevent.

The official narrative blamed Bowser for the assassination. But the subtext blamed the Rakasha—if Peach hadn't formed an inappropriate attachment, if the Rakasha hadn't tempted her, if the boundaries had been respected, none of this would have happened. The conspiracy that murdered Peach also murdered the possibility of Rakasha-Kingdom integration.

For eighty-five years, the Rakasha have existed at the margins of a Kingdom that destroyed one of their own (the child) and devastated their chief (Thornpaw). They watched the civil war consume Kingdom society. They maintained their borders while the Kingdom bled.

Thornpaw's silence during this period—his refusal to speak about Peach until the gala—may have been protective. Speaking would have invited retaliation against his people. The confession of love would have been read as confession of motive. Better to stay silent and let the Kingdom destroy itself.

Now, with the Kingdom fractured and the Regency weakening, Thornpaw has spoken. The timing suggests calculation as much as catharsis. The Rakasha are positioning themselves for whatever comes next.

## Current Relevance — Why the Rakasha Matter Now

The Rakasha matter to the current crisis for several reasons:

**Dimensional Expertise:**

The Planar Fracture has created instability that conventional approaches cannot address. Spirit-walkers have capabilities that may be essential to resolution—or to exploitation. Any faction seeking to address the dimensional crisis should be courting Rakasha cooperation.

**The Secret Heir:**

If Thornpaw's child survived—if a half-Rakasha heir to the Mushroom Kingdom exists somewhere—the Rakasha presumably know their location. This heir would be approximately eighty-five years old, raised in Rakasha traditions, connected to Rakasha power structures. Their emergence would transform everything.

**Alternative Power Center:**

As the Kingdom collapses, the Rakasha represent an alternative power structure—one that has maintained stability while others have failed. Their confederation governance, their spiritual traditions, their territorial integrity all suggest a society that WORKS when others are falling apart.

**Intelligence Capability:**

Spirit-walkers can perceive across dimensional boundaries. They can communicate through means that conventional surveillance cannot intercept. The Rakasha intelligence network may be the most sophisticated in the region—and the most difficult for other factions to penetrate.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Rakasha are playing a long game.

For eighty-five years, they have watched the Mushroom Kingdom—the society that rejected integration with them—tear itself apart. They have maintained their strength while others weakened. They have kept their secrets while others exposed themselves.

Now, at the moment of maximum Kingdom weakness, Thornpaw has revealed the secret that makes the Rakasha central to the assassination narrative. This is not coincidence. This is strategy.

Waluigi respects strategic patience. Waluigi has waited for his moment many times—waited for the perfect serve, the ideal shot, the opening that turns competition into victory. The Rakasha have been waiting for eighty-five years. Their moment may be approaching.

What they will DO with that moment—whether they seek justice, revenge, integration, or something else—remains to be seen. But they will not be ignored. They cannot be marginalized anymore.

The people beyond the eastern forests are coming into focus. The Kingdom should pay attention.

WAH.

name: Toadsworth the Elder
title: The Chamberlain Who May Have Betrayed Everything
status: Deceased — died approximately 1020 BF under circumstances that vary by source
affiliation: Mushroom Kingdom Royal Palace (Former Chamberlain) / Mushroom Regency (Acting Regent, later Regent Emeritus)
summary: Toadsworth the Elder was the Royal Chamberlain at the time of Princess Peach's assassination and the person who became Acting Regent in the chaos that followed. His private journals—allegedly recovered by Loyalist operatives in 1010 BF—contain references to 'the arrangement,' 'the timing,' and apparent confessions of enabling the assassination without personally committing it. If the journals are authentic, Toadsworth Sr. is one of history's greatest traitors—a man who facilitated the murder of the monarch he was sworn to protect. If the journals are forgeries, he is a victim of posthumous character assassination by the very terrorists who destabilized the kingdom. The Regency claims forgery. The Loyalists claim authenticity. Waluigi claims UNCERTAINTY, because Waluigi has learned that convenient evidence should be examined carefully regardless of which side presents it. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Toadsworth the Elder with appropriate caution, because this figure is central to the most disputed aspect of the assassination narrative.

## The Official Record — Loyal Servant

The Regency's official history presents Toadsworth Sr. as a devoted public servant who stepped into leadership during the kingdom's darkest hour.

According to this narrative:

- Toadsworth Sr. served as Royal Chamberlain for over thirty years under Princess Peach, managing palace operations with distinction.
- When the Princess was assassinated, he organized the initial response—securing the scene, coordinating the investigation, maintaining order in the capital.
- He became Acting Regent because the Council of Toads needed experienced leadership and he was the most qualified available.
- He guided the kingdom through the early civil war, making difficult decisions under impossible circumstances.
- He eventually stepped back to 'Regent Emeritus' status, allowing his son (the current Chancellor Toadsworth) to assume primary leadership.
- He died as a respected elder statesman, mourned by those who understood his sacrifices.

This narrative presents a man who did his duty when duty was hardest. A servant who became a leader because leadership was needed.

## The Loyalist Accusation — Architect of Murder

The Loyalist narrative is dramatically different.

According to their interpretation of the recovered journals:

- Toadsworth Sr. was approached by conspirators approximately six months before the assassination and offered a choice: prevent the killing or enable it.
- He chose enablement. He created the guard rotation gap—the forty-seven-minute window during which no guards protected the Royal Suite.
- He did not personally commit the murder, but he made the murder POSSIBLE. Without the gap, the assassin could not have reached the Princess.
- After the assassination, he controlled the investigation—ensuring evidence was suppressed, witnesses were eliminated, and the official narrative blamed Bowser rather than actual conspirators.
- He became Regent because the chaos he helped create provided the opportunity.
- He spent the remainder of his life protecting the conspiracy that gave him power.

This narrative presents a man who betrayed everything for ambition. A servant who became a ruler by murdering his monarch.

## The Journals — Authentic or Fabricated?

Everything depends on the journals' authenticity.

The journals were allegedly recovered by Captain Toadette's operatives in 1010 BF during an infiltration of Regency archives. The Loyalists claim they found the journals in a sealed vault, separate from official records—exactly where a guilty man would hide evidence of his crimes.

The Regency claims the journals are sophisticated forgeries created by Loyalist propagandists. They point to:

- **Handwriting inconsistencies** — Analysis by Regency-employed experts found variations from verified Toadsworth Sr. documents.
- **Anachronistic references** — Some passages allegedly reference events or terminology that did not exist during the journal's supposed composition dates.
- **Convenient timing** — The 'discovery' occurred during a period of intensified Loyalist military activity, when propaganda value was highest.
- **Chain of custody** — The journals passed through Loyalist hands before any independent examination. Opportunity for fabrication existed.

The Loyalists counter:

- **Handwriting variation is normal** — People's handwriting changes over time, especially under stress. Variation proves nothing.
- **Anachronism claims are exaggerated** — Regency 'experts' are motivated to find problems. Independent analysis shows no definitive anachronisms.
- **Timing reflects opportunity** — Loyalists found the journals when they penetrated the archives. Discovery timing reflects access, not fabrication.
- **Chain of custody criticism is circular** — The Regency cannot examine evidence they claim is fabricated without admitting the evidence exists to examine.

Waluigi has not personally examined the journals. Waluigi has seen reproductions, but reproductions can be fabricated from fabrications. Without access to originals and independent verification, Waluigi cannot determine authenticity.

## Key Passages — What the Journals Allegedly Say

Assuming the journals are authentic (a significant assumption), they contain passages that implicate Toadsworth Sr. in the conspiracy:

**'The timing was arranged. The positions were cleared. What happened after was not my doing, but I made it possible.'**

This suggests Toadsworth Sr. created opportunity (the guard rotation gap?) without personally committing violence. He enabled without executing.

**'They approached me with the arrangement six months prior. I had a choice: prevent it and remain a servant, or allow it and become a ruler. God forgive me.'**

This describes a direct offer—complicity in exchange for power. The 'God forgive me' suggests guilt, or at least awareness that the choice was morally catastrophic.

**'The Guild provided the method. The Regency provided the opportunity. I do not know who held the blade. Perhaps that ignorance is my only mercy.'**

This implicates the Mages' Guild as co-conspirators who provided 'the method'—possibly the magical capabilities needed to kill the guards or disable the wards. It also suggests Toadsworth Sr. did not know the assassin's identity, which would explain why that identity remains secret.

**'My son inherits what I built. He inherits the secrets with it. I pray he has the wisdom to maintain what I could not destroy.'**

This suggests Chancellor Toadsworth (the current Regent) knows about the conspiracy and is actively maintaining the cover-up. The son inherited not just power but complicity.

## The Death — Suspicious or Natural?

Toadsworth Sr. died approximately 1020 BF. The circumstances vary by source:

**Regency version:** Natural causes. He was elderly and had been in declining health. He died peacefully, surrounded by family.

**Loyalist version:** Murdered. Someone—possibly within the Regency itself, possibly the Mages' Guild—eliminated him before he could be captured and made to testify. His journals were meant to be destroyed with him; the fact that they survived was an oversight.

**Third possibility:** Suicide. Toadsworth Sr., knowing the Loyalists were closing in and unwilling to face either capture or assassination, chose to end his own life. The journals were left deliberately as a confession.

Waluigi cannot determine which version is accurate. The death was convenient for those who wanted the conspiracy protected. It was also convenient for those who wanted a martyr figure. Convenient deaths should be examined carefully regardless of who benefits.

## Chancellor Toadsworth — The Son's Inheritance

Chancellor Toadsworth—the current Regent—is Toadsworth Sr.'s son. If the journals are authentic, the passage about 'my son inherits what I built' implicates him in ongoing cover-up.

The Chancellor's behavior supports this interpretation... or doesn't, depending on perspective:

- He has maintained the Regency's denial that the journals are authentic.
- He has suppressed investigation leads that might expose the conspiracy.
- He has maintained relationships with the Mages' Guild and the Iron Legion—both implicated in various aspects of the assassination and its aftermath.

All of this could indicate active cover-up participation. It could also indicate a son defending his father's reputation against what he genuinely believes are terrorist fabrications.

The Loyalists recently seized Toad Town and placed Chancellor Toadsworth under house arrest. If they interrogate him about his father's journals, answers may finally emerge.

Or the answers may be whatever the Loyalists want them to be. Coerced testimony is not reliable testimony.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Toadsworth Sr. is either:

1. **A guilty conspirator** whose journals reveal his complicity in murdering the monarch he served. His power was built on betrayal, and his son continues the cover-up.

2. **An innocent victim** of posthumous character assassination. The journals are forgeries created by terrorists who needed a villain, and his reputation was destroyed to justify their violence.

3. **Something more complicated** — Perhaps he was coerced into participation. Perhaps he knew about the conspiracy but did not enable it as directly as the journals suggest. Perhaps some journal passages are authentic and others are interpolated fabrications.

Waluigi cannot determine which is true.

What Waluigi CAN say: the guard rotation gap exists in official records. Something caused that forty-seven-minute absence. If it wasn't Toadsworth Sr., who was it? The gap requires explanation. The journals provide one. If the journals are fabricated, an alternative explanation is needed.

No alternative has been convincingly provided.

Waluigi will continue investigating. The truth about Toadsworth Sr.—guilty architect or innocent scapegoat—is central to understanding what actually happened eighty-five years ago.

WAH.

name: The Unknown Assassin
title: The Blade That History Cannot Name
race: Unknown — possibly Human based on partial evidence
status: Unknown — alive, dead, or something else depending on which theory you believe
affiliation: Unknown — connected to 'the arrangement' if it existed
summary: Someone killed Princess Peach on Highsun 1, 955 BF. That person's identity remains the central mystery of the assassination—the question that eighty-five years of investigation, propaganda, and civil war have failed to answer. The official narrative blamed Bowser, but the evidence is weak and Bowser has denied involvement consistently. Lady Bloomia's testimony claims the killer's identity is recorded in Princess Peach's list—'someone the Princess loved,' in the third column headed 'HELD THE BLADE.' If Bloomia exists and her testimony is accurate, she knows the answer. If she is fictional or fabricating, the mystery persists. Waluigi has encountered numerous theories about the assassin's identity. None are proven. All are disturbing in different ways. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the unknown assassin as a separate entry because the killer's identity is CENTRAL to everything and yet remains completely unresolved. This person—whoever they are—committed the act that broke the kingdom. Understanding them is essential to understanding the crime.

## What We Know About the Killing

The assassination method provides limited information about the killer:

**The Wound:**

Princess Peach was killed by a single blade wound through the base of her skull. The precision suggested medical knowledge or supernatural guidance. No blood was spilled on her white dress. She was found seated at her vanity, holding a hairbrush, as if she had simply stopped mid-motion.

The precision implies SKILL. This was not a frenzied attack. It was a calculated strike designed to kill instantly and cleanly.

**The Entry:**

The assassin entered through the secret hatch—the hidden passage behind the portrait of Queen Portabella that Princess Peach had shown to Chief Thornpaw. This implies KNOWLEDGE. Someone knew about the hatch and shared that information with the killer... unless the killer was someone who already knew.

**The Guards:**

Four elite Toad Guards were found dead at their posts, killed by 'simultaneous cessation of all biological function'—a spell so advanced that fewer than five practitioners were believed capable of casting it. This implies MAGICAL CAPABILITY or magical assistance.

**The Exit:**

The assassin departed through the same hatch, leaving a partial bloody handprint on the stone. Lady Bloomia's testimony (if authentic) describes this handprint as 'too large for a toad, too small for a koopa. A HUMAN handprint.'

This suggests the assassin was HUMANOID and approximately human-sized. Not a Koopa, despite the official narrative.

## The Theories — Who Might Have Done It?

Waluigi has encountered numerous theories about the assassin's identity. Each has supporters and problems:

**Theory One: A Professional Assassin**

The simplest explanation. Someone hired a professional killer—skilled, anonymous, untraceable. The conspirators (whoever they were) contracted the murder to someone whose specialty was making people die quietly.

Supporting evidence: The killing's precision suggests professional training. The lack of identification after eighty-five years suggests effective anonymity.

Problems: Professionals leave trails. Payment records. Handler contacts. Reputation networks. Eighty-five years of investigation should have produced SOMETHING.

**Theory Two: A Mages' Guild Operative**

The Guild killed the guards. Perhaps a Guild operative also killed the Princess. The magical precision of both killings suggests the same capability source.

Supporting evidence: The guard-killing spell was extremely advanced—Guild-level magic. If the Guild was involved in the conspiracy, using their own operative for the final act maintains containment.

Problems: Guild operatives are KNOWN. Their identities, while protected, are not perfectly secret. Someone should have recognized the killer if they were Guild.

**Theory Three: Chief Thornpaw**

The most uncomfortable theory. Thornpaw knew about the hatch. Thornpaw had access to the chambers. Thornpaw could have committed the killing and then feigned ignorance for eighty-five years.

Supporting evidence: Access and opportunity. The human-sized handprint is consistent with Rakasha physiology (some Rakasha are human-sized). Thornpaw's eighty-five years of silence could indicate guilt rather than grief.

Problems: Motive is unclear. Why would Thornpaw kill the woman he loved? Unless the relationship soured, or he was coerced, or the 'love' story is itself fabrication.

**Theory Four: Someone from Peach's Inner Circle**

Bloomia's testimony says the killer was 'someone the Princess loved.' This suggests not a stranger but someone KNOWN to Peach. A friend. A confidant. A family member.

Supporting evidence: Peach was found peaceful—not struggling, not defensive. She may have ALLOWED the killer to approach because she trusted them.

Problems: Who in Peach's inner circle would commit murder? And why?

**Theory Five: Princess Peach Herself**

The darkest theory. Peach arranged her own death. She chose her killer. She sat at her vanity and waited because the death was consensual—a sacrifice rather than a murder.

Supporting evidence: Bloomia's testimony suggests Peach KNEW the assassination was coming and prepared for it. The 'loved' description could mean Peach chose someone she trusted to perform an act she had requested.

Problems: Why would Peach want to die? Martyrdom? Protection of her child? Despair? The theory raises as many questions as it answers.

**Theory Six: Mario**

Waluigi hesitates to even document this theory, but it exists, so Waluigi must acknowledge it.

Mario was sent abroad before the assassination—deliberately removed, according to conspiracy theories. But what if his removal was COVER? What if Mario committed the killing and then established an alibi by being 'abroad'?

Supporting evidence: Mario had unique access to Peach through years of service. He could approach her without triggering alarm. His subsequent investigation could have been performance—hunting for a killer he knew didn't exist because HE was the killer.

Problems: This theory requires Mario to be a murderer, which contradicts everything known about his character. It requires the most heroic figure in the kingdom's history to be its greatest villain. Waluigi finds this implausible in the extreme.

But Waluigi notes the theory exists. Others have considered it. The uncomfortable possibilities must be documented.

## The Third Column — Bloomia's Knowledge

If Lady Bloomia exists and her testimony is accurate, she knows the killer's identity.

Princess Peach's list—recovered from the leather case—allegedly contains three columns: 'KNEW,' 'HELPED,' 'HELD THE BLADE.' The third column contains only one name. Bloomia claims to know this name but refuses to reveal it without supporting evidence.

She describes the killer as 'someone the Princess loved' and says 'it is not the name anyone expects.'

This phrasing eliminates obvious suspects. If the name is unexpected, it's probably not Bowser, not a known Guild operative, not a recognizable figure from the conspiracy theories.

Someone unexpected. Someone loved. Someone who held the blade.

Who fits this description?

## The Partial Handprint — Physical Evidence

The bloody handprint on the hatch stone is the only physical evidence of the killer's identity.

Bloomia's testimony describes it as human-sized. The official investigation apparently found the handprint but—according to Loyalist claims—'somehow missed it' or cleaned it or lied about it.

If the handprint exists in any form—preserved evidence, photographs, detailed descriptions—it could provide identification. Handprints are distinctive. Comparison analysis could match or exclude suspects.

The Loyalists presumably have access to Bloomia's description. Whether they've attempted handprint comparison is unknown.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Waluigi does not know who killed Princess Peach.

Waluigi has documented the theories. Each has supporters. Each has problems. None are proven.

What Waluigi believes:

- The killer was probably human or human-sized humanoid (based on handprint).
- The killer had knowledge of the secret hatch (either through Thornpaw, through Peach herself, or through other means).
- The killer was skilled enough to strike with lethal precision.
- The killer may have been someone Peach knew and trusted (based on lack of defensive posture).
- The killer has never been identified despite eighty-five years of investigation.

The last point is significant. Secrets that important should not survive eighty-five years. Someone should have talked. Someone should have been caught. Someone should have left evidence that was followed to conclusion.

Unless the killer is dead. Or the killer is protected by powers that maintain the cover-up. Or the killer is someone whose exposure would be so devastating that even investigators prefer not to find them.

The unknown assassin remains unknown. The blade that killed a kingdom remains unnamed.

Waluigi finds this UNACCEPTABLE. Mysteries should have solutions. Crimes should have perpetrators. Justice should be possible.

Waluigi will continue investigating.

WAH.

name: Chancellor Toadsworth
title: The Son Who Inherited Everything
status: Active — under house arrest following Loyalist seizure of Toad Town
affiliation: Mushroom Regency (Current Chancellor) / Toadsworth Family Legacy
summary: Chancellor Toadsworth is the current head of the Mushroom Regency and the son of Toadsworth the Elder—the man whose journals allegedly confess to enabling Princess Peach's assassination. If those journals are authentic, the Chancellor inherited not just power but COMPLICITY. His father's final written words reportedly state: 'My son inherits what I built. He inherits the secrets with it.' The Chancellor has spent his career maintaining the Regency's official narrative, suppressing investigation leads, and continuing relationships with the Mages' Guild and Iron Legion—both implicated in various aspects of the assassination and its aftermath. He is either a man desperately protecting his father's reputation against terrorist fabrications, or a man actively perpetuating an eighty-five-year cover-up. Captain Toadette's Loyalists recently placed him under house arrest. What they extract from him—through interrogation, coercion, or whatever methods Toadette considers appropriate—may finally answer questions that have haunted the kingdom for generations. Waluigi is not optimistic that the truth will emerge cleanly. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Chancellor Toadsworth with acknowledgment that this individual may be central to resolving the assassination mystery—or may be a victim of circumstance whose only crime is having the wrong father.

## The Inheritance — Power and Secrets

Chancellor Toadsworth did not seize power. He INHERITED it.

His father, Toadsworth the Elder, served as Royal Chamberlain under Princess Peach and became Acting Regent after her assassination. The elder Toadsworth guided the Regency through the early civil war, established the administrative structures that persist today, and eventually stepped back to allow his son to assume primary leadership.

The transition was presented as natural succession—father to son, mentor to protégé, experienced hand to trained replacement. The Regency framed it as continuity and stability during chaotic times.

If the Loyalist interpretation of the elder Toadsworth's journals is correct, the transition was something else entirely: the passing of conspiracy from one generation to the next. The father enabled an assassination. The son maintains the cover-up. The family business is treason dressed as governance.

The Chancellor has never publicly acknowledged the journals' existence, let alone their contents. The Regency's official position is that the documents are sophisticated forgeries created by terrorists to justify violence. Whether the Chancellor believes this—or merely says it—Waluigi cannot determine.

## The Chancellor's Tenure — Patterns of Behavior

Chancellor Toadsworth's time in office has been characterized by several consistent patterns:

**Investigation Obstruction:**

Every attempt to reopen inquiry into Princess Peach's assassination has been blocked, delayed, or redirected by Regency officials under the Chancellor's authority. Requests for access to sealed archives are denied. Witnesses who come forward are discredited or disappear. Investigative leads are declared 'exhausted' without adequate exploration.

His defenders argue this represents reasonable governance—refusing to indulge terrorist propaganda, maintaining focus on current crises rather than historical grievances. His accusers argue it represents active cover-up.

**Mages' Guild Cooperation:**

The Chancellor has maintained close relationships with the Mages' Guild—the organization allegedly complicit in the assassination according to Loyalist theories. Guild operatives have privileged access to Regency facilities. Guild recommendations carry unusual weight in policy decisions. The Chancellor has never publicly criticized Guild actions, even when those actions proved controversial.

This cooperation could indicate conspiracy. It could also indicate political pragmatism—the Guild is powerful, and alienating them would be strategically unwise regardless of historical grievances.

**Iron Legion Arrangements:**

Financial records recovered by the Loyalists allegedly show payments between the Iron Legion and Regency officials—including documents bearing the Chancellor's signature. The relationship appears to involve territorial agreements, resource sharing, and what Toadsworth the Elder's journals called 'the arrangement.'

If the Legion is funding the Regency and the Regency is protecting the Legion, both organizations benefit at the kingdom's expense. This would be corruption even without assassination conspiracy. WITH the conspiracy connection, it suggests the cover-up has institutional support from multiple directions.

## The House Arrest — Current Situation

Captain Toadette's Loyalists seized Toad Town on Day 12 of the current crisis. Among their actions: placing Chancellor Toadsworth under house arrest.

The Chancellor is reportedly confined to his residence, guarded by Loyalist operatives, awaiting... something. Interrogation? Trial? Summary execution? The Loyalists have not announced their intentions. Captain Toadette does not explain her plans to outsiders.

What the Loyalists might extract from the Chancellor:

- **Journal authentication** — Confirmation that his father's journals are genuine
- **Conspirator names** — Identification of current officials involved in ongoing cover-up
- **Evidence locations** — Sealed archives, hidden documents, protected witnesses
- **The killer's identity** — If the Toadsworth family knows who struck the fatal blow

What the Loyalists might PRODUCE regardless of truth:

- **Coerced confession** — Torture produces compliance, not accuracy
- **Propaganda testimony** — Statements that serve Loyalist purposes regardless of accuracy
- **Martyrdom** — If the Chancellor dies in custody, he becomes either a Regency martyr or proof of Loyalist justice, depending on who tells the story

Waluigi does not expect clean resolution. The Loyalists have waited eighty-five years for this opportunity. They will not waste it on careful jurisprudence.

## The Personal Question — What Does He Know?

The central question about Chancellor Toadsworth is whether he KNOWS the truth.

**If he knows his father enabled the assassination:** Every action of his career takes on darker meaning. The investigation obstruction is cover-up. The Guild cooperation is conspiracy maintenance. The Legion payments are corruption funding.

**If he believes his father was innocent:** His actions might represent genuine defense of family honor against terrorist slander. The obstruction is protecting legitimate governance from destabilization.

**If he suspects but doesn't know:** Perhaps the most tragic possibility. A son who has noticed inconsistencies, encountered evidence that doesn't fit, but chosen not to investigate because the answers might be unbearable. Willful ignorance as coping mechanism.

Waluigi cannot determine which scenario is accurate. Only the Chancellor's private thoughts—and whatever the Loyalists extract—might reveal the truth.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Chancellor Toadsworth is either a villain maintaining his family's conspiracy or a victim of his family's reputation. Either way, his position is untenable.

If the journals are authentic, he has perpetuated treason for decades. Justice demands accountability.

If the journals are fabricated, he has been framed for crimes his father did not commit. Justice demands vindication.

Neither outcome is likely to be delivered cleanly. The Loyalists are not interested in fair process. The Regency is not capable of objective investigation. The kingdom's institutions are too broken to provide legitimate judgment.

What happens to Chancellor Toadsworth depends on Captain Toadette's intentions, the Loyalists' discipline, and factors Waluigi cannot predict.

Waluigi hopes the truth emerges. Waluigi doubts it will satisfy anyone.

WAH.

name: Mistveil
title: The Loyalist Who Extracts Secrets
status: Active — operating undercover in various capacities
summary: Mistveil is one of Captain Toadette's most effective intelligence operatives—a specialist in infiltration, extraction, and the acquisition of secrets that powerful people prefer to keep hidden. At Fawful's gala, Mistveil posed as a minor noble and extracted Chief Thornpaw's confirmation of his relationship with Princess Peach—testimony that validated decades of Loyalist theories. The conversation lasted approximately thirty minutes and produced more actionable intelligence than some operatives gather in years. Waluigi respects professional excellence even when it serves factions whose methods disturb him. Mistveil is professionally excellent. Mistveil is also absolutely dedicated to Captain Toadette's vision, which means Mistveil is DANGEROUS in ways that go beyond mere competence. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting Mistveil based on operational reports and secondhand accounts. Intelligence operatives are not inclined to share their methods, and Mistveil is reportedly among the most security-conscious of the Loyalist cadre.

## The Operative — What Is Known

Mistveil's name is presumably a cover identity. Whether the individual behind the name is male, female, or something else varies by report—suggesting either deliberate obfuscation or the use of multiple operatives under a single codename.

What is consistent across accounts:

**Infiltration Expertise:** Mistveil can adopt personas convincingly enough to pass in hostile environments. The gala operation required posing as minor nobility among factions that would kill a Loyalist operative on sight. Mistveil succeeded.

**Extraction Capability:** Getting information FROM people is Mistveil's specialty. The Thornpaw conversation was not an interrogation—Thornpaw chose to speak. Mistveil created conditions where speaking felt natural, safe, appropriate.

**Absolute Dedication:** Mistveil is a true believer. The Princess's memory is sacred. Captain Toadette's leadership is legitimate. The Loyalist cause is just. This dedication makes Mistveil effective... and unpredictable.

## The Gala Operation — Thornpaw Extraction

Mistveil's most documented operation was the intelligence extraction at Fawful's gala.

The operational challenge: Fawful's event brought together representatives from hostile factions under a volatile host's supervision. Loyalist presence would be detected and eliminated if discovered. Yet the intelligence opportunity was too significant to ignore—Chief Thornpaw was attending, and Thornpaw potentially held information about the assassination that no one else possessed.

Mistveil infiltrated the gala as a minor noble of unclear origin. The cover identity apparently passed multiple layers of scrutiny. Mistveil mingled, observed, and eventually approached Thornpaw during a lull in formal proceedings.

The conversation lasted approximately thirty minutes. By its conclusion, Thornpaw had confirmed:
- His secret relationship with Princess Peach
- His knowledge of the secret hatch in her chambers
- The existence of their child
- His belief that the assassination was motivated partly by preventing a half-Rakasha heir

This testimony validated theories the Loyalists had promoted for decades. Whether Mistveil's skill drew out truth or Thornpaw was simply ready to speak, the operation was a decisive intelligence success.

## Methods — The Uncomfortable Question

Mistveil extracts information. The question Waluigi cannot answer is HOW.

Some extraction is simply skillful conversation—creating rapport, asking the right questions, making people comfortable enough to share. Mistveil clearly possesses these skills.

But Loyalist intelligence operations have historically included less gentle methods. Captain Toadette's faction does not hesitate to use coercion, threats, or violence when they consider it necessary. The Bramblehaven massacre demonstrates their willingness to accept casualties.

Does Mistveil employ harsher methods? Has Mistveil tortured sources? Killed witnesses after extraction? Used threats against families or communities?

Waluigi does not know. The Loyalists do not publish operational guidelines. What Waluigi knows is that Mistveil serves an organization whose moral boundaries are... flexible.

## The Network — Not Operating Alone

Mistveil is not the only Loyalist intelligence operative. Captain Toadette commands a network that has gathered information across the kingdom for decades:

- **Embercap** leads field operations
- **Bloodcap** handles what Waluigi assumes are violent assignments
- **Stonecap** manages logistics
- **Archivist Inkwell** discovered the guard rotation gap in 998 BF

Mistveil's specialty is human intelligence—getting people to talk. Others in the network handle signals intelligence, document recovery, and the elimination of obstacles.

Together, they have accumulated evidence that now threatens to collapse the Regency entirely.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Mistveil is exactly what Waluigi would want in an intelligence operative: skilled, dedicated, effective, capable of operating in environments that would destroy lesser agents.

Mistveil is also exactly what Waluigi fears in a Loyalist: true belief that justifies any action, dedication that permits any atrocity, effectiveness in service of an organization whose methods include massacre.

The Thornpaw extraction was professional excellence. But professional excellence in service of Captain Toadette means professional excellence that might include things Waluigi does not want to contemplate.

Waluigi respects Mistveil's capability. Waluigi does not trust Mistveil's organization. The distinction matters.

WAH.

name: Merric
title: The Axe-Wielding Sheep Who Joined the Team Because Why Not
status: Active — recruited during the Shadow Estate rooftop escape after calling Markop “Centerus”
affiliation: Shadow Estate escape party / new Disaster Inc.-linked ally
summary: Merric is an axe-wielding sheep encountered during the Shadow Estate sequence. He behaved as if he was already part of the team, then failed Markop’s identity check by calling him “Centerus,” then accepted the correction not by apologizing but by joining the team for real. Waluigi respects this recruitment method because it is fast, confusing, and paperwork-light.
description:
Merric entered the record during the Shadow Estate upper-floor chaos as a sheep with an axe and enough confidence to critique Markop's violence. During the rooftop escape sequence, the party finally asked who he actually was. Merric's answer pattern established two facts: he did not know Markop's name, and he was willing to become part of the team anyway.

## The Sheep With An Axe

The Shadow Estate has produced ghosts, vampires, a medusa, a beastmaster, singing servants, and a shapeshifter at the exit, so an armed, opinionated, self-appointed teammate in the shape of a sheep is, by local standards, almost reasonable. Merric arrived behaving as though he had always been part of Disaster Inc., offered live commentary on Markop's fighting technique, and generally conducted himself with the serene confidence of someone who has never once doubted his own belonging.

## The Centerus Incident

The party eventually attempted to verify this newcomer. Markop asked Merric what his name was. Merric answered "Centerus"—which was wrong, being neither his name nor Markop's. Markop, rather than pressing the point, asked why Merric did not simply join their team instead. Merric thought about it and said sure, why not. Waluigi files this as the cleanest recruitment in Disaster Inc. history: no oath, no interview, no paperwork, just a sheep agreeing to a stranger's suggestion mid-crisis.

## A Worrying Kind Of Simple

Waluigi respects Merric's recruitment method because it is fast, confusing, and paperwork-light—all qualities Waluigi values in principle. He remains wary in practice, because "we acquired a heavily armed ally who does not know our names and joined on a whim during a rooftop escape" is the sort of sentence that reads as convenient right up until it does not. For now, Merric wields his axe on the correct side of the fight, which is all Waluigi asks of anyone.

name: Tanukiburt
title: The Toadburt-Shaped Problem at the Portal Circle
status: Active — discovered at the Shadow Estate portal circle with Mystic Morel and the injured real Toadburt
affiliation: Shadow Estate portal-circle hostiles / enemy wildcard
summary: Tanukiburt is the newest and least welcome answer to the Toadburt question: a Tanuki-shaped or Toadburt-shaped problem found at the master-bedroom portal circle alongside Mystic Morel and the injured real Toadburt. Waluigi does not yet know the full mechanics. Waluigi does know that if a person named Tanukiburt is standing next to the real Toadburt at the only exit, the correct response is screaming followed by tactical planning.
description:
Tanukiburt was confirmed during Remi's scouting after the Mirror of True Reflection was repaired. Looking into the master bedroom from outside, Remi saw Tanukiburt, the real injured Toadburt, and Mystic Morel gathered around the portal circle while the rug was being manipulated. This places Tanukiburt at the party's immediate route home and makes him a direct obstacle to activating the Midnight Fountain or using the portal safely.

## The Toadburt Question, Made Worse

For a while the Toadburt situation was a straightforward missing-person problem: the Iron Legion's coerced operative had slipped free of his entropy ring and gone to work for the Shadow Estate's Archivist in exchange for healing, and the party simply wanted to know where he had gone. Tanukiburt's appearance detonated that simplicity. Standing beside the real, injured Toadburt is a second Toadburt-shaped figure, which converts a location problem into an identity problem—and identity problems, Waluigi notes, cannot be solved with a tennis racket.

## Shapeshifter At The Door

Everything about Tanukiburt's staging is hostile. He is at the portal circle. He is beside Mystic Morel, the singing prophet-thief who opens planar doorways. He is between Disaster Inc. and the only known exit. Whether Tanukiburt is a Tanuki impersonator, a magical duplicate, or some other trickster construct is unresolved, but the placement is unambiguous: he is a guard on the last threshold.

## Current Threat Meaning

Tanukiburt's presence means the Toadburt situation is no longer just "where is Toadburt?" It is now "which Toadburt, why are there two, and how many of them are standing between the party and home?" A shapeshifter guarding the exit is the specific nightmare that turns every rescue into an interrogation. Waluigi hates riddles that stand in doorways.

name: Vaxillus the Beastmaster
title: The Taxidermy Enthusiast Remi Used as a Ladder
status: Active — pursuing the party with Lyranth after the mirror recovery; unwillingly used as Remi’s ladder
summary: Vaxillus the Beastmaster is a Shadow Estate pursuer whose current confirmed role includes waving from below, threatening the party with taxidermy-adjacent intentions, being used by Remi as a biological ladder, and then carrying Lyranth into the second story so the hunt could continue upward. Waluigi dislikes him but admits the ladder part was funny.
description:
Vaxillus entered the immediate Shadow Estate escape record as part of the exterior pursuit after Remi discovered the occupied portal circle. He and Lyranth did not appear to be trying to petrify the party. They appeared to prefer stuffing them into taxidermy, which Waluigi considers a distinction without comfort.

## A Different Kind Of Threat

The Shadow Estate is full of ways to die, and Vaxillus represents one of its more disturbing specialties. Where the medusa Lyranth turns victims to stone, Vaxillus's threat is taxidermy-adjacent—the promise of being preserved, posed, and displayed rather than merely killed. Waluigi has cataloged many hazards in this encyclopedia. "Will stuff you and mount you on a wall" ranks high on the list of fates a person should sprint away from.

## The Biological Ladder Incident

Vaxillus's confirmed contributions to the escape sequence include waving from below, threatening the party, and—memorably—being used by Remi as a living ladder. During the attempt to reach the roof, Remi climbed him like scaffolding, prompting a guard to yell, "HEY, BE CAREFUL WITH THAT THING." Waluigi believes this is the first known Estate safety warning ever issued on behalf of a hostile pursuer being climbed by a fourteen-year-old with an urgent schedule.

## Ally To The Hunt

After the climb, Vaxillus carried Lyranth into the second story so the pursuit could continue upward, cementing his role as a mobile piece of the Estate's hunting apparatus rather than a lone predator. Waluigi dislikes him on principle—he is, after all, trying to turn the party into decor—but concedes that the ladder part was genuinely funny, and that this encyclopedia would be poorer without the phrase "biological ladder incident" in it.

name: Rattles
title: The Skeleton Who Wants His Old Body Back
status: Active — escaped the Shadow Estate rooftop by grabbing onto Remi during Feather Fall
affiliation: Shadow Estate escape party / recruited local ally
summary: Rattles is a skeleton recruited from a servant closet who wants to turn back time and regain his original flesh-and-bones body, not a replacement. He speaks with deeply skeleton-appropriate timing, joined the party during the Shadow Estate servant corridor sequence, and survived the rooftop escape by grabbing onto Remi during Feather Fall.
description:
Rattles first entered the record during the servant corridor investigation, where he was found with an antique frog and a goblet. He wanted his old body back specifically, which Waluigi finds unusually precise for a skeleton in a closet.

## A Very Specific Wish

Most reanimated skeletons, in Waluigi's experience, want either revenge, rest, or someone's soul. Rattles wants something oddly technical: to turn back time and regain his original flesh-and-bones body—not a replacement, not an upgrade, the exact one he had before. This precision suggests Rattles remembers being alive clearly enough to be picky about it, which makes him less a monster and more a person filing a very difficult complaint with the universe.

## Recruited From A Closet

Rattles joined the party during the Shadow Estate servant corridor sequence, arriving with an antique frog and a goblet like a man who had been interrupted mid-errand a very long time ago. He speaks with deeply skeleton-appropriate timing, which Waluigi will not define further except to say that the delivery lands. He fit into Disaster Inc. immediately, on the grounds that a group this chaotic barely notices one more improbable member.

## Recent Update — Feather Fall Escape

During The Mirror, the Roof, and the Fall, Rattles remained with the rooftop group while Lyranth, Vaxillus, ghosts, guards, and singing servants turned the upper estate into a death box. When the escape came, he grabbed onto Remi and descended safely under Feather Fall. Waluigi notes that "skeleton survives fall by holding onto a child with a magic feather" is legally a sentence but emotionally a problem, and files it under the growing list of things the Shadow Estate has made normal.

name: Salam
title: The Liberated Toad Who Escaped the Roof / Salem Eye-Shot Alias
status: Active — merged Salam/Salem file; escaped the Shadow Estate rooftop with Remi’s Feather Fall chain; Spider Grove eye-shot record retained here
affiliation: Liberated Toads / Shadow Estate escape party / Disaster Inc. situational ally
summary:
Salam is one of the Liberated Toads caught in the Shadow Estate disaster sequence. His newest confirmed contribution is simple and important: he survived the rooftop trap by grabbing onto Remi during the Feather Fall evacuation before Lyranth, Vaxillus, ghosts, and guards could convert the roof into a display case.

Merged note: the old Salem file has been folded into Salam. The Spider Grove eye-shot record and the Shadow Estate rooftop escape now live under this canonical Salam profile.

Former Salem summary: Salem is the crossbow specialist who landed an incredible shot through the Arachnid Matriarch's primary eye cluster during the Battle of the Spider Grove. The shot threaded through a titan-scale grapple between Markop and the Matriarch, struck a target the size of a dinner plate at sixty feet, and contributed directly to the creature's destabilization. Waluigi acknowledges this was an EXCELLENT shot and gives credit accordingly, even though Waluigi's arcane rays ALSO contributed to the victory and arguably deserve equal recognition.
description:
Salam’s detailed personal file remains thinner than Waluigi would prefer, but the Shadow Estate has a way of turning minor participants into urgent ledger entries.

## Recent Update — Feather Fall Escape

During The Mirror, the Roof, and the Fall, Salam was part of the group that escaped the rooftop with Remi’s Feather Fall. This confirms him as active in the current Shadow Estate escape party and still alive as of the descent to the grounds.

## Merged Salem Record

Salem operated from an elevated position in the surviving trees during the Spider Grove battle, providing ranged support while the ground forces dealt with swarms and Markop wrestled the Matriarch at titan scale. Waluigi did not have extensive interactions with Salem during the battle—they were both focused on their respective roles—but the crossbow bolt that pierced the Matriarch's eye cluster spoke louder than conversation.

## The Shot

The Arachnid Matriarch was thirty feet across, her legs spanning gaps between trees like organic bridges. Markop had her in a titan-scale grapple, both of them straining against each other while the ground churned beneath them. The fight was chaotic, violent, and constantly moving.

Salem's crossbow bolt threaded through this chaos. It passed between grappling limbs, avoided the environmental destruction, and struck the Matriarch's primary eye cluster—multiple eyes grouped together, the closest thing to a vulnerable point on a creature built like an armored nightmare.

The shot was EXCEPTIONAL. Waluigi has excellent aim through decades of athletic competition, and he's not sure he could have made that shot. The distance, the movement, the chaos, the precision required—Salem delivered under conditions that would have caused most shooters to miss entirely.

## Combat Role

Salem's role in engagements appears to be precision ranged support. While others engage directly—Markop grappling, Waluigi providing arcane rays, Remi holding defensive positions—Salem finds elevated angles and waits for shots that matter. This requires patience, judgment, and the discipline to not fire until the moment is right.

Waluigi respects this. Waluigi's own approach is more... expressive. He attacks when attacks are needed, provides support across the engagement, and makes his presence KNOWN through sustained magical output. Salem's approach is quieter, more focused, and produces singular moments of devastating effectiveness rather than consistent pressure.

Both approaches are valuable. The Spider Grove victory required ALL of them—Markop's grappling, Waluigi's rays, Salem's precision shot, Remi's defensive holding, the Oracle's banishment circle. Nobody won that fight alone.

## Assessment

Waluigi does not know Salem's current status. The Planar Fracture scattered everyone, and Waluigi has not been able to confirm which dimension Salem ended up in or whether Salem remained in the physical world. The crossbow and its wielder could be anywhere.

Waluigi hopes Salem is alive and still shooting. The party will need precision capability when they reunite. Giant spiders are not the only threats out there, and some of those threats will have vulnerable eye clusters that need piercing.

If Salem ever reads this: that was a GOOD shot. Waluigi gives credit where credit is due. Not often, but when deserved.

WAH.

name: Rodger
title: The Toad Who Keeps Asking For Inventory While Everyone Else Invents Brand Crimes
status: Active — co-leading the Liberated Toads with Toad Lee and trying to keep the survivors functional
summary: Rodger is one of the practical leaders of the Liberated Toads: the sort of survivor who asks about food, medicine, watches, lists, guard rotations, and whether anyone has checked on the injured while the louder people argue about destiny, revenge, or party branding. Waluigi respects this because civilization is mostly paperwork performed under stress.
description:
Rodger became important during the Vigilance crisis because he represented the boring, necessary miracle of organization. While others seized control, made speeches, panicked, or caught fire morally and literally, Rodger tried to keep the Liberated Toads alive as people rather than symbols.

## Logistics As Heroism

Rodger's entire method can be summarized as asking the unglamorous question at the worst possible moment. When the Vigilance descended into chaos, the loud voices asked who should lead. Rodger asked who had checked on the injured, whether the watches were covered, and where the food was going. Waluigi has watched enough disasters to know that the person counting bandages is usually the reason anyone survives to argue about destiny afterward. Rodger is that person, and he is exhausted about it.

## The Faction's Spine

Where Speaker L supplies vision and Toad Lee supplies lore, Rodger supplies the thing that keeps a traumatized barrel-community from disintegrating: routine. Guard rotations. Inventory. Lists. He backed the practical faction during the internal crises that nearly tore the Liberated Toads apart, and he has spent every crisis since trying to convert fear into function. It is not inspiring work. It is the work that makes inspiring work possible.

## The Naming Dispute

Rodger has no patience for the fight over whether the party is Disaster Inc., the Freeroamer Heroes, or the Freeloader Zeros. His stated position is that any name is acceptable if the people arguing about it also carry crates, count bandages, and stop blocking the hallway. When the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute spilled into the Liberated Toads and became public morale theatre, Rodger's contribution was to request that the theatre be moved somewhere that was not the supply corridor. Waluigi finds this reasonable and therefore politically doomed.

name: Teacher T
title: The Lesson-Plan Survivor
status: Active — Liberated Toad organizer and member of the Class of T
summary: Teacher T is one of the named Liberated Toads who rallied around Rodger during the Vigilance crisis. Teacher T thinks names matter because names become what frightened people repeat when they need courage. This has made Teacher T dangerously involved in the Disaster Inc. naming dispute.
description:
Teacher T survived the barrel trafficking horror and emerged with the deeply inconvenient belief that language should help people understand what is happening to them. Waluigi respects this academically while noting that most of the current situation resists lesson planning.

## The Instinct To Explain

Teacher T's response to catastrophe is not to fight it or flee it but to make it comprehensible. During and after the Vigilance crisis, Teacher T became the voice that turned raw horror into something a frightened community could hold in its head—naming what had happened, framing why, and insisting that people who understand their situation are harder to break than people who merely fear it. In a movement of survivors, this is not a soft skill. It is triage for the mind.

## Names As Weapons And Comforts

Teacher T's central conviction is that names matter because names become what frightened people repeat when they need courage. A good name steadies a shaking hand; a cruel one lodges in a child's mouth and stays there. This belief has dragged Teacher T, somewhat unwillingly, into the middle of the kingdom's pettiest and most persistent argument.

## Naming Position

Teacher T dislikes "Freeloader Zeros" because children might repeat it. Teacher T considers "Freeroamer Heroes" aspirational but possibly dishonest. Teacher T accepts "Disaster Inc." as historically accurate but wants a footnote explaining that accuracy is not endorsement. Within the Disaster Inc.
