Naming Dispute, this makes Teacher T the closest thing the argument has to a conscience—which is precisely why nobody louder listens. Waluigi grudgingly approves the footnote.

name: Bully T
title: The Toad Who Weaponized Heckling For Morale
status: Active — Liberated Toad survivor and Class of T loudmouth
summary: Bully T is a Liberated Toad whose survival strategy appears to involve saying the thing that makes the most powerful person in the room angriest, then acting like this was tactical morale support. Waluigi does not endorse this method. Waluigi does understand it.
description:
Bully T backed Rodger during the faction's internal crisis and has since become one of the voices most likely to turn fear into noise. Sometimes that noise is useful. Sometimes it is just noise.

## The Weaponized Heckle

Bully T's survival strategy is unusual: say the thing that makes the most powerful person in the room angriest, then act as though this was tactical morale support all along. In the right moment, a well-aimed insult can shake a frightened crowd out of paralysis, puncture a tyrant's aura, or simply remind exhausted people that defiance is still an option. In the wrong moment, it is a Toad yelling at a general for no strategic reason whatsoever. Waluigi does not endorse this method. Waluigi does understand it.

## Morale By Provocation

Where Teacher T steadies people with understanding and Rodger steadies them with routine, Bully T steadies them with attitude—the loud, contagious refusal to be impressed by anyone's power. During the Liberated Toads' internal crisis, this made Bully T a reliable amplifier of whatever the practical faction needed the room to feel. It is a blunt instrument, but blunt instruments have their uses when the alternative is silence.

## Naming Position

Bully T calls the group Disaster Inc. whenever Archie can hear it, the Freeroamer Heroes whenever Waluigi can hear it, and the Freeloader Zeros whenever Wario is already mad enough that one more insult will not change the invoice. Within the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute, Bully T is not a partisan—he is an opportunist who has realized that all three names are equally effective at getting a rise out of somebody. This is not diplomacy. It is sport.

name: Nerd T
title: The Spreadsheet Toad of Brand Warfare
status: Active — Liberated Toad analyst and Class of T record keeper
summary: Nerd T is one of the Liberated Toads now tracking the Disaster Inc. naming dispute with charts, tallies, legal notes, faction reactions, and a growing confidence that nobody involved should be allowed near branding decisions.
description:
Nerd T supported Rodger during the Vigilance crisis and then made the mistake of proving useful with records. Once you prove useful with records, Waluigi notices. This is both an honor and a curse.

## The Archivist Nobody Asked For

Nerd T's contribution to the Liberated Toads is memory made rigorous. Where the community remembers its ordeal in feeling—the barrels, the Iron Legion, the fires Dan set—Nerd T remembers it in columns: who was aboard, what was traded, which numbers do not add up. In a movement forced into politics before it was ready, having someone who writes things down accurately is a quiet form of power, because the faction that controls the record controls the argument about what happened.

## Data Under Duress

What elevates Nerd T from clerk to combatant-of-a-different-kind is the refusal to let a crisis excuse sloppy accounting. Even during the Vigilance disaster, Nerd T kept tallying, on the theory that survivors would eventually need to prove what was done to them. Waluigi respects this. Evidence, unlike courage, does not fade when the adrenaline does.

## Naming Position

Nerd T has calculated that "Disaster Inc." has the strongest evidentiary accuracy, "Freeroamer Heroes" has the highest morale uplift, and "Freeloader Zeros" has the highest invoice correlation. Nerd T refuses to pick a winner until more data arrives, tracking the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute with charts, tallies, legal notes, and faction reactions, and a growing confidence that nobody involved should be allowed near branding decisions. Waluigi says the data already arrived and it says Waluigi was first.

name: Geek T
title: The Button-Maker of the Naming War
status: Active — Liberated Toad tinkerer, morale crafter, and Class of T menace
summary: Geek T is a Liberated Toad who saw three competing names for one disaster party and immediately began thinking about badges, signs, tablets, slogans, and possible merchandising. Waluigi is horrified. Wario is interested. This is the worst possible combination.
description:
Geek T survived the Vigilance and attached themself to the Liberated Toads' practical recovery work, mostly by fixing small things, labeling supplies, and turning morale into objects people can hold. This is useful. It is also how the naming dispute acquired physical merchandise.

## The Maker

Geek T is the Liberated Toads' quiet engineer of everyday function—the one who repairs the latch, labels the crate, and converts abstract community feeling into tangible, hold-in-your-hand objects. In a survivor community, this matters more than it sounds. A frightened person who is handed something solid and useful feels, briefly, that the world can still be fixed. Geek T manufactures that feeling on a small scale, one repaired object at a time.

## Merchandising A Disaster

The gift becomes a hazard when applied to the naming argument. Geek T saw three competing names for one disaster party and immediately began thinking about badges, signs, tablets, slogans, and merchandise. Waluigi is horrified. Wario is interested. Waluigi considers "horrified Waluigi plus interested Wario" the worst possible combination of reactions any idea can provoke.

## Naming Position

Geek T has made prototype buttons for Disaster Inc., the Freeroamer Heroes, and the Freeloader Zeros. The Disaster Inc. button is purple and legally superior. The Freeroamer Heroes button is heroic and annoyingly popular. The Freeloader Zeros button sold out first because Wario bought them all to hand out with bills. In this way Geek T single-handedly turned the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute from a verbal quarrel into a physical economy, which Waluigi regards as an escalation that history will not forgive. WAH.

name: Archie Archbold Miser
title: The Indebted Pyromaniac Who Bleeds Entropy
status: Active — Magic restored but unstable; Financially ruined; Carrying too many secrets; Currently at Raventree Manor with Luigi and Mages' Guild operatives / Missing — Last seen leaving a watch in a grove
affiliation: Disaster Inc. / Mages' Guild (coerced employee, effective immediately, no severance package)

summary: Archie Miser is the middle child of a single mother raising five children. Born with a mysterious third eye on his forehead—the origin of which remains unknown even to him—Archie spent 25 years under his family's rigid control with little personal choice. He served 5 years as a grunt in his city's watch before being promoted to castle watchman at a faraway castle, where he worked for 4 years. Despite the better pay and acceptable conditions, Archie felt trapped—viewing his promotion as golden handcuffs rather than recognition. Everything changed when he discovered he could use magic during his tenure. Magic became his liberation: a force of whimsy and power that made him feel alive for the first time. When he left his position and attempted to return home, a self-defense fireball incident forced him to stand trial and shattered his plans. Knowing his family would harshly punish him for abandoning their rigid expectations, Archie chose freedom instead. Now a beginner mage with a strong moral compass, he intends to live life on his own terms—helping others, protecting the innocent, and targeting evil—while enjoying himself until and beyond his final days. Archie Miser is the 'spark' that started the current fire. A leader of the scattered Disaster Inc. group, he is currently missing, though his presence is felt through the objects he left behind—specifically a watch found near a grove in the Shadow Estate. A letter addressed to him suggests he is being hunted by both 'The Guild' and 'The Hand.'
description:
Waluigi has spent more words documenting Archie Miser than any other individual in this encyclopedia, and Waluigi STILL doesn't feel like the documentation captures the full scope of the man's capacity for generating problems. Archie doesn't create disasters intentionally. He creates them the way storms create lightning—through the accumulation of volatile conditions until discharge becomes inevitable.

## The Man Before the Crisis — Origins and Family

Archie Miser is the middle child of a single mother household consisting of five siblings: an older brother (the eldest), an older sister, Archie himself, a younger sister, and a younger brother (the youngest). The Miser family enforced a life of rigidity upon Archie for 25 years, allowing him little to no personal choice in any matter. His upbringing was strict, controlled, and suffocating.

The third eye on Archie's forehead is something he was born with. The origin remains a complete mystery—even to Archie himself. Whether it was inherited from unknown ancestry, magically generated, a genetic abnormality, or something else entirely is left open to interpretation. What IS certain is that the third eye has always been part of him, marking him as different from birth.

## Career: From City Watch to Castle Watchman

Archie served in the city watch of his hometown for 5 years, remaining a grunt throughout his entire tenure despite years of service. Eventually, he received a promotion to work as a watchman at a faraway castle, a position that came with higher pay.

He worked at this castle job for 4 years. The pay was good. The work environment was acceptable. The tasks were manageable. Everything was FINE.

But Archie wanted more. He felt deeply dissatisfied despite the fancy title. To him, the job was just another cage—a gilded one, perhaps, but a cage nonetheless. He even suspected his promotion was golden handcuffs: a way to keep him compliant and trapped rather than genuine recognition of his abilities.

## The Magical Awakening

Everything changed when Archie discovered he could use magic during his tenure as castle watchman.

For the first time in his rigidly controlled life, Archie felt ALIVE. Magic represented something his years of dutiful service never provided: wonder, agency, and possibility. To Archie, magic is a force of both whimsy and power—a spectacle that makes people stop and awe at its splendor, and a supernatural tool that serves as both protection and weapon.

By the time of his departure from his watchman position, Archie was a beginner mage. Capable, but still learning the true extent of his abilities.

## Departure and the Fireball Incident

When Archie finally left his castle position, he initially intended to return home to his family. Those plans fell apart catastrophically.

Archie was forced to cast a fireball in self-defense. The incident led to a trial. His homecoming was derailed by legal troubles—but more importantly, Archie knew what awaited him if he returned. His family would harshly punish him for abandoning the rigid life they had enforced upon him for 25 years. Returning home meant surrendering the freedom he had only just begun to taste.

So Archie made a choice. Rather than face his family's judgment and lose his newfound independence, he chose to forge his own path.

## Current Philosophy and Moral Compass

Archie is determined to maintain his newfound freedom and live life to the fullest—now and beyond the end of his days. He refuses to return to the cage his family represents.

Despite his desire for personal freedom and enjoyment, Archie possesses a strong moral compass. He chooses to do good in the world, albeit in his own unconventional way:

- Helping other people in need
- Ensuring the safety of various groups
- Targeting genuinely evil individuals

Archie will continue to enjoy himself while making a positive difference—on his own terms, in his own way.

## The Three-Eyed Bandit

Archie's underworld alias originated from a heist that went wrong in ways that only Archie's heists go wrong. He attempted to steal a cursed artifact—Waluigi does not know the specifics and frankly does not WANT to know—and the artifact's defensive enchantments temporarily granted him precognitive flashes. For a brief period, Archie could see moments into the future.

Did this make him MORE effective? NO. It made him MORE RECKLESS, because Archie interpreted 'I can see danger coming' as 'I can walk directly into danger and dodge at the last second.' The alias stuck even after the precognition faded, which tells you everything about how the underworld perceives Archie: as someone touched by strange magic, unpredictable, and best approached with caution.

Waluigi thinks the alias is appropriate. Archie does seem to have a third eye—except instead of seeing the future, it sees the nearest flammable object.

## Recent History: Rakka, Pirates, and Ravencreek

Before the current crisis, Archie was operating under the direction of a mysterious entity called Rakka, working from a hidden temple deep in the enchanted woods. Waluigi has heard RUMORS about Rakka—that they're a sorceress, a spirit, a fey entity, a collector of forbidden knowledge—but nothing concrete. What IS concrete is that Rakka employs agents for dangerous retrieval missions, and Archie was one of those agents.

During this period, Archie worked alongside pirates—specifically the Sea Dogs smuggling crew—and an unidentified 'horse person' whose nature Waluigi cannot even BEGIN to speculate about. His activities took him to Ravencreek, a town in the Midlands that exists under the shadow of vampire-werewolf conflict.

In Ravencreek, Archie stayed at the Veilwood Spa—a luxurious establishment secretly operated by vampires from Fairth's Retreat. He apparently paid with unusual foreign currency and used the alias 'Mr. Ash,' which is the most OBVIOUS fake name Waluigi has ever heard. 'Mr. Ash.' The fire mage. Called himself 'Mr. ASH.' Waluigi cannot decide if this is stupidity or audacity, and with Archie, it's probably both.

During Archie's stay, Ravencreek suffered a werewolf attack. Whether Archie was involved in provoking this attack, defending against it, or simply present while it happened is unclear from the available evidence. What IS clear is that he left Ravencreek shortly afterward and returned to Rakka's Temple.

## The Swiftsoul Incident

On Efferd 26th, 1040 BF, an explosion at Swiftsoul Air Blimp Station killed three people and caused significant property damage. Archie Miser was arrested for the crime after a pursuit through service corridors that ended with him jumping onto a cliffside ledge in apparent desperation.

The prosecution's case seems straightforward: Archie's magical signature was found at the blast site, witnesses saw him fleeing, and his history of fire magic makes him a natural suspect.

BUT.

The evidence, when examined closely, tells a different story:

- Archie was TELEPORTED to Swiftsoul Station from Rakka's Temple, arriving in a panicked state. He did not choose to be there at that moment.
- The magical residue analysis shows only a 'Grade D' match to Archie's signature, with 65% uncertainty due to interference patterns and metallic contamination.
- Archie was DRUGGED with Nightshade Bloom extract (a Class III paralytic/hallucinogen) approximately 1-2 hours before his capture. Someone incapacitated him deliberately.
- Faint tracking glyphs were observed on his arms during medical treatment—glyphs that match Iron Fists Guild control runes.
- The Iron Fists Guild had access to Platform 3 via suspicious override codes, and their communications reference a 'Burn Notice' protocol and ensuring Archie's 'situation resolved cleanly.'
- The cargo on the damaged blimp was 'Volatile Alchemical Reagents' destined for Edgeshade—the town that was recently destroyed by dragons.

Waluigi believes Archie was framed. The Iron Fists Guild—possibly working with or against Wario, possibly connected to Archie's work for Rakka—arranged for Archie to be present at the explosion as a convenient scapegoat. They drugged him, tracked him, and let the investigation focus on the obvious fire mage while the true perpetrators cleaned up their evidence.

This does NOT mean Archie is innocent of everything. His ledger shows payments from Rakka, dealings with pirates, and a concerning entry about 'W - Emergency Extraction Fund' that suggests he knew about Wario's schemes. But the Swiftsoul explosion specifically? Archie was the patsy, not the perpetrator.

## The Tea Party Incident

Waluigi has documented the Tea Party Incident extensively elsewhere, but it bears repeating in the context of understanding Archie as a person: when a diplomatic meeting devolved into a three-faction brawl, Archie's solution was to cast a fireball. In a cargo hold. On a wooden airship. Full of people.

The fact that the ship didn't explode and kill everyone is either a miracle or evidence that the universe wants to see what Archie does NEXT. The fact that Archie has never expressed remorse for the fireball—only ANNOYANCE that people keep bringing it up—tells Waluigi everything he needs to know about Archie's relationship with consequences.

## The Darman Knightly Persona

Archie survived the Shadowfell dinner party by operating under a false identity: Darman Knightly. This persona allowed him to navigate vampiric politics without immediately being identified as the fire-throwing maniac who destabilizes everything he touches. The cover required Archie to be calm, measured, and NOT set things on fire, which Waluigi imagines was physically painful for him.

The cover's requirements escalated to the point where Archie was forced to cut off Usk's finger to prove his loyalty to the vampire lords. He DID IT. He actually cut off a friend's finger to maintain a disguise. Waluigi understands the tactical necessity—the cover was keeping him alive in a room full of vampires—but understanding necessity doesn't mean FORGIVING the act. Usk is missing a finger. Archie took it. That equation doesn't balance no matter how much context you add.

## Current Status

Archie is currently trapped in the Shadowfell alongside Bowser, which Waluigi considers cosmically appropriate. The Shadowfell suppresses fire magic through planar physics, meaning Archie—whose entire approach to existence depends on fire—is operating in a dimension specifically designed to neutralize his primary capability.

He is also, technically, a wanted fugitive in the Midlands, facing charges of murder, manslaughter, reckless endangerment, and property destruction. The prosecutor, Miles Edgeworth, apparently has a near-perfect conviction rate. If Archie ever returns to the physical world and the Midlands' jurisdiction, he will need an EXCELLENT lawyer.

Waluigi would feel sorry for Archie if Archie hadn't contributed to the Planar Fracture through his unstable magical contributions to the Oracle's ritual. The ritual required stable magical energy. Archie provided Archie-flavored energy, which is to say volatile, fire-adjacent, and about as stable as a house of cards in a hurricane. When the ritual collapsed, Archie's magic was part of the collapse.

## Assessment

Archie Miser is brilliant, dangerous, and completely unable to exist in the world without leaving scorch marks. He is also, Waluigi grudgingly admits, an effective ally in combat situations that REQUIRE fire. During the Spider Grove battle, knowing that Archie's firepower would be available for the Matriarch fight (if he'd been there) was strategically relevant. Markop claimed the War Mage's Staff on Archie's behalf, which means Archie will eventually have EVEN MORE fire capability, which Waluigi finds concerning but also acknowledges is probably necessary given the threats they're facing.

Archie is also, apparently, the victim of a sophisticated framing operation by the Iron Fists Guild, which makes him sympathetic in ways Waluigi did not expect. Someone ELSE caused the Swiftsoul explosion. Someone ELSE killed those people. Archie was drugged, teleported, tracked, and blamed because he was convenient—a known fire mage with underworld connections and a history of not thinking before casting.

Waluigi's official position on Archie: stand at least thirty feet away during any conversation that might go badly. Given Archie's track record, that's ALL conversations. But also maybe help him find a lawyer, because the charges against him are WRONG, and even Archie doesn't deserve to be executed for someone else's crimes.

WAH.

Archie owes debts to half the kingdom. He doesn't even know about the ones being owed TO him.

## The Vigilance — Where Things Started Going Wrong

Archie's involvement in the current crisis began aboard the Vigilance—the airship that served as a mobile theater of escalating catastrophe.

During the Tea Party Incident and subsequent Syndicate Showdown, Archie deployed fireballs in enclosed spaces aboard a WOODEN AIRSHIP. The explosions killed most of the Tea Leaf Syndicate's muscle and contributed to the cascade of events that saw the Syndicate destroyed, Earl Grey literally explode, and Green T dragged through a mirror dimension.

Archie's defenders—and there are a FEW—argue that the fireballs were cast in self-defense during situations where conventional responses had failed. His critics—and there are MANY—argue that casting fireballs inside a wooden ship full of civilians represents reckless endangerment so extreme that it borders on criminal negligence.

The Onyx Hand tribunal that acquitted him of killing Stormweave did so on grounds of justifiable defense. Whether the same tribunal would have acquitted him for the Vigilance fires is a question nobody has tested, possibly because nobody wants to examine the civilian casualty numbers too closely.

Waluigi's assessment: Archie did not INTEND to cause mass casualties. Archie's intentions are rarely the problem. The problem is that Archie's instinctive response to threat is FIREBALL, and fireball is not a precision instrument. It is a blunt force solution applied to problems that may or may not require blunt force, and the collateral damage is someone else's problem.

## The Iron Sky Breach — Archie's Interrogation

When the Iron Legion boarded the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach, Archie was among those who encountered Legion operatives directly.

During this period, Archie was interrogated by an Iron Legion agent—reportedly named Agent Malissia—who attempted to extract information about the Oracle. During the interrogation, Archie managed to snap off the 'handler' half of a paired Entropy Ring system.

This broken ring half became one of Archie's most significant possessions. The Entropy Ring system was the mechanism by which the Iron Legion had coerced Toadburt into becoming a sleeper agent—the handler ring transmitted commands, the paired ring on Toadburt received and enforced them. By breaking the handler piece away, Archie gained the ability to sense active Entropy Rings within range and—once per day—jam their signal, potentially giving Toadburt one moment of free will.

Whether Archie ever successfully used this capability to free Toadburt is unclear. The chaos of subsequent events may have prevented it. But the fact that Archie—in the middle of an interrogation, while being threatened by a military intelligence operative—had the presence of mind to sabotage the enemy's control mechanism demonstrates something important about him.

Archie is not stupid. Archie is not incompetent. Archie is CHAOTIC in ways that make people assume incompetence, but underneath the fireballs and the debt and the property damage, there is a mind that recognizes critical objectives and acts on them.

Waluigi does not often praise Archie. But the Entropy Ring gambit was smart. Possibly the smartest thing Archie has ever done.

## The Planar Fracture — Cast Into Shadow

The Planar Fracture scattered Disaster Inc. across three hostile dimensions. Archie and Bowser were cast into the Shadowfell—the plane of shadow, entropy, and vampires who consider dinner guests to be literal dinner.

Archie woke up on a marble floor in a world drained of all color. Black. White. Shades of grey. No warmth. No light beyond cold white flames that produced no heat. Windows showing bruised purple clouds and petrified trees.

And his fire was GONE.

The Shadowfell's entropy consumed magical energy. When Archie tried to snap a flame into existence—his most basic, instinctive ability—nothing happened. Snap after snap. A tiny spark appeared and instantly died. He tried a fireball. Nothing. Just a puff of cold grey smoke.

Waluigi has documented Archie's relationship with fire throughout this encyclopedia. Fire is not merely Archie's weapon. It is his IDENTITY. The way Waluigi is defined by athletic excellence and justified grievance, Archie is defined by his ability to make things burn. Take away Waluigi's tennis racket and Waluigi is still Waluigi. Take away Archie's fire and Archie is... what?

A man in a grey dimension with no magic, no allies except a giant turtle, and no plan except 'play along and hope the vampires don't eat me.'

Bowser, naturally, found this hilarious. 'Looks like you're out of fuel, candle-man.'

Waluigi LOVES the nickname 'candle-man.' Waluigi would never say this to Archie because Archie would fireball him. But Waluigi is documenting his love of this nickname for posterity.

## The Shadow Estate — Surviving Without Fire

Forced to rely on actual wits instead of explosions, Archie demonstrated capabilities that his fire magic usually overshadows.

**Disguise and Deception:**

Archie disguised himself as a vampire guard, choosing the painfully uncreative alias 'Dracacide.' Later, when interacting with actual Purple Legion vampires near a crashed airship, he adopted the name 'Vin.' Neither alias was convincing by any reasonable standard, but they WORKED—because the vampires' social structure assumed anyone following protocols belonged. Archie exploited this assumption with the instincts of someone who has been getting into places he shouldn't be his entire life.

He navigated vampire bureaucracy. He filed PAPERWORK to maintain cover—the vampires apparently required incident reports even for routine activities. He convinced a vampire guard that a missing prisoner had escaped in a direction Archie had deliberately led them away from. He talked his way through checkpoints, past suspicion, around questions that should have blown his cover.

Archie without fire is not helpless. He is DIFFERENT. The fire burns away subtlety—why be clever when you can be explosive? Without it, the cleverness emerges. The survival instincts sharpen. The man who resolves problems with fireballs reveals that he can also resolve them with words, deception, and quick thinking.

Waluigi does not know if Archie realizes this about himself. The fire returned eventually, and Archie went right back to using it as his primary tool. But the Shadowfell proved that Archie Miser contains multitudes, even if most of those multitudes are on fire.

**The Purple Legion and the Crashed Airship:**

Archie encountered what appeared to be Iron Legion forces operating in the Shadowfell—except they called themselves the 'Purple Legion' and ruled a territory called 'the Vamp Lands.' They were scrapping a crashed airship named the Deliverance and had taken prisoners, including someone who appeared to be Dan.

Archie—still disguised as 'Vin'—infiltrated the crash site. He talked his way past guards, formed an impromptu 'investigation party' with actual vampire soldiers, and gathered intelligence about the Purple Legion's operations. He obtained a MAP that he recognized as the Midlands—but purple-tinted, shadowfell-reflected.

The prisoner identified as Dan escaped before Archie could reach him. A mysterious figure named Orvinder Danos—a barrister who appeared from nowhere, walked with a cane he didn't need, and seemed to know Archie by name—offered assistance and access to a portal leading back to the ruined manor.

Archie's instinctive response to a stranger who knows his name and offers portal access was SUSPICION. Good instincts. Orvinder proved to be genuinely helpful—a man of strict honesty and justice according to Archie's character assessment—but the suspicion was warranted. In the Shadowfell, trust is currency that spends fast and refunds never.

**The Wandering — A Month in the Forest:**

Archie and Green T were separated multiple times during the Shadow Estate events. After the dinner party catastrophe and the Anchor shattering, after the various encounters with vampires and crashed airships, Archie lost track of Green T and spent TIME—significant time—trying to find him.

He returned to the vampire manor looking for Green T. Green T wasn't there. He explored the surrounding territory. He checked the tavern. He asked questions. He searched.

He didn't find Green T.

Archie spent approximately a MONTH living in the forest outside the Shadow Estate, alone, in a dimension that suppressed his magic and drained color from reality. A month of isolation in the Shadowfell, where the eternal grey wears on sanity the way water wears on stone—not through force but through relentless, unceasing pressure.

When Archie finally returned to the manor, it 'flashed'—the walls crumbled, and he found himself back in the mirror room of the ruined material-plane Raventree Manor. As if the Shadowfell had finally decided to spit him out.

A month alone in the plane of shadow. Waluigi has difficulty imagining this. Waluigi is a social creature—Waluigi NEEDS an audience, even if the audience is just Toad Lee trying to navigate fairy court obligations. A month of solitude in a dimension designed to extinguish hope would test anyone.

Archie survived it. Archie came out the other side. The man who panicked when his fire disappeared adapted to a world without fire and lived in it for WEEKS. Whatever else Waluigi says about Archie—and Waluigi says a LOT—the man does not give up. The man does not stop. The man endures.

## The Mages' Guild — Archie's New Employers

When Archie emerged from the Shadowfell back into the material plane at Raventree Manor, the Mages' Guild was waiting.

Two Guild operatives—identified in various sources as Agent L and a spy—had Archie surrounded. Their conversation revealed disturbing intelligence:

**'You're the reason the portal unexpectedly opened.'**

Archie's magical signature is described by the Guild as 'bleeding entropy.' His magic is not merely powerful—it is UNSTABLE in ways that affect dimensional boundaries. His presence at Raventree Manor contributed to the planar instability that defined the crisis. His magic didn't just cast spells—it leaked destructive energy that weakened reality around him.

This is simultaneously terrifying and validating. Terrifying because it means Archie is a walking planar hazard. Validating because it means the Planar Fracture was not ENTIRELY the Oracle's ritual failure—Archie's entropy contributed. The shushing of Waluigi's concerns during the ritual was even MORE unjustified than Waluigi thought.

**The Toadburt Revelation:**

The Guild operatives confirmed what Archie's broken Entropy Ring had suggested: Toadburt was an Iron Legion sleeper agent, equipped with an Entropy Ring, tasked with capturing the Oracle. The Guild had an 'arrangement' with the Iron Legion regarding this—they had allowed the sleeper agent to operate because it served Guild interests.

Archie's shock at learning Toadburt's status was genuine: 'Toadburt is your sleeper agent?!' The Guild's willingness to sacrifice an innocent Toad for operational convenience is consistent with their institutional behavior throughout the crisis.

**The Oracle's Bridge Plane:**

The Guild operatives revealed that the Oracle had constructed a 'Regulator Plane'—a Bridge Plane connecting the Shadowfell, Feywild, and Material planes. The Oracle intended to use this bridge to collapse the connections, severing the fractured dimensions from each other.

The implications are staggering. The Oracle is not merely guiding the party through the crisis—they are actively constructing dimensional infrastructure for purposes that may or may not align with anyone else's survival.

**'You work for the Mages' Guild now.'**

The Guild's ultimatum was blunt: Archie's 'immense power comes with immense responsibility and oversight.' The Guild would oversee his activities 'from afar.' He didn't have a choice.

Archie's response—'Wait, what?'—captures the helplessness of someone who has been outmaneuvered by bureaucracy. You can fight vampires. You can survive dimensional fractures. You cannot fight an institution that has decided you are now on their payroll.

The Guild's 'oversight' is not protection. It is CONTROL. They want Archie contained—his entropy managed, his movements monitored, his capabilities directed toward Guild objectives. The man who killed their operative Valorian Stormweave now works for the organization Stormweave served.

Irony is not strong enough a word.

## Luigi — The Unlikely Partner

The Guild introduced Archie to his new partner by shouting for someone to come in. A bump was heard at a nearby door. It opened.

Luigi.

The brother of the kingdom's greatest missing hero, armed with a vacuum cleaner, working a ghost-clearing contract for the organization implicated in the assassination of the woman his brother spent his career protecting.

Archie and Luigi's partnership at Raventree Manor is one of the most unlikely pairings in the campaign. The pyromaniac and the ghostbuster. The man who creates chaos and the man who cleans it up.

Luigi's combat style—fear-based, vacuum-centric, punctuated by missed fireballs and frantic screaming—is the opposite of Archie's aggressive approach. When confronted by a Waltzgeist in the ruined dance hall, Luigi clapped his hands, sparked a green fireball, MISSED, got punched by a ghost, and then frantically vacuumed the entity out of the air while Archie provided covering fire that also missed.

Their partnership is not elegant. But it FUNCTIONS. Luigi handles the ghosts. Archie handles the threats that aren't ghosts. Thornbury handles the paperwork and charges everyone for everything.

## Thornbury and the Rope — 2,062 Gold Pieces

Thornbury. The Mages' Guild quartermaster-spy who traveled with Archie and Luigi through the ruined manor, tracking expenses with the dedication of an accountant who believes fiscal responsibility is a moral imperative.

When Thornbury's fifty-foot hempen rope snapped under Archie's weight as he tried to climb to an upper floor, Thornbury produced an itemized bill:

- Guild Membership Levy: 50 gp
- Master Weaver's Inspection: 200 gp
- Arcane Certification Seal: 150 gp
- Ogre Load-Test Certification: 300 gp
- Environmental Impact Assessment: 75 gp
- Quality Assurance Audit: 100 gp
- Expedited Processing Fee: 250 gp
- Administrative Stamp & Wax: 40 gp
- Hazardous Material Surcharge: 80 gp
- Inflation Adjustment: 100 gp
- Guild Master's 'Discretionary Gratuity': 500 gp
- Sales Tax: 217 gp 5 sp

**Grand Total: 2,062 gold pieces and 5 silver.**

Waluigi wept tears of JOY reading this bill. The Mages' Guild are bureaucratic extortionists, and Waluigi respects the sheer GRIFT of charging a man two thousand gold for a broken rope. The 'Ogre Load-Test Certification'—they dropped an ogre from a city wall seven times to test the rope. The 'Guild Master's Discretionary Gratuity'—for his new wyvern saddle. The 'Hazardous Material Surcharge'—because the rope MIGHT be used for climbing.

Archie is now financially ruined. He owes more for a broken rope than most people earn in a year. The Guild agent laughed and walked off. Archie said he'd pay for it, which Waluigi interprets as either remarkable optimism or complete detachment from financial reality.

## The Overheard Conversation — Acceptable Deaths

While exploring the manor with Luigi and Thornbury, Archie climbed a rope to an upper floor and listened in as Agent L and another Guild operative discussed the planar fracture.

The conversation was partly encrypted—fragments of code interspersed with plain language. But the plain language portions were devastating:

**'Even if it may kill Archie?'**

**'Yes.'**

The Guild was willing to let Archie die. The ghost-clearing operation that would destabilize the planar fracture further was proceeding regardless of whether Archie survived the process. His entropy-bleeding magic made him useful AND expendable—a tool whose destruction was factored into operational planning.

Archie heard this. He heard the people who now EMPLOY him discussing his acceptable death with the same casual tone used for budget line items.

And then the rope snapped.

## Mystic Morel — The Purple Toad Who Stole Everything

The Purple Toad—later identified as Mystic Morel, a fortune teller who speaks in rhyming prophecies and apparently has the sticky fingers of a master pickpocket—appeared while Archie was recovering from injuries sustained in a library ambush.

Morel SANG to Archie. A full musical number called 'Shuffle the Deck, Dear Hero' that combined fortune-telling metaphors with cryptic intelligence about the Oracle's plans, Peach's heir, and the nature of the planar crisis. Waluigi has obtained partial lyrics:

*'The Heir was grown, not born, you see—Root and scale in tapestry. Cut the vine or cut the thread? Either way... something's dead.'*

This verse may reference Princess Peach's half-Rakasha child. 'Grown, not born' could mean the heir was raised in hiding rather than acknowledged publicly. 'Root and scale'—Rakasha traits. 'Cut the vine or cut the thread'—a choice between destroying the evidence or destroying the heir.

While singing, Morel STOLE Archie's watch, keys, and other items from his bag. Archie—injured, held down by Luigi and the Guild guard—could not prevent the theft.

Then Morel used Archie's own compass and tools to open a PLANAR PORTAL. Right there. In the room. Using items from Archie's pocket.

'Have you ever seen a planar portal open where it never was meant to?' Morel asked.

He stepped through the portal. It closed.

Archie's possessions were used to tear a hole in reality. The items he carried—his compass, his tools—were apparently capable of enabling dimensional transit when operated by someone who knew how. Morel knew how. Archie did not.

This raises disturbing questions about what Archie has been carrying, where those items came from, and whether Archie's entire journey has been manipulated by forces that provided him with dimensional tools disguised as ordinary equipment.

## The Burden of Knowledge — What Archie Carries

Archie currently carries two massive secrets that affect the entire party:

**Secret One: Toadburt's Entropy Ring.**

Archie holds the cracked handler half of the Entropy Ring system. He knows Toadburt is a coerced sleeper agent. He knows the Iron Legion forced the ring onto Toadburt and programmed him to capture the Oracle. Archie has kept this secret from the party, hoping to use the handler ring to jam the signal and free Toadburt.

The ethical weight of this secret is considerable. Every moment Archie keeps quiet, Toadburt remains enslaved. But revealing the secret might trigger Toadburt's programming—or might cause the Iron Legion to activate backup protocols. Archie is frozen between action and inaction, knowing that both carry terrible risks.

**Secret Two: The Oracle's Bridge Plane.**

Archie learned from the Guild spies that the Oracle has constructed a Bridge Plane connecting the three dimensional fragments. The Oracle may intend to collapse this bridge, severing the planes permanently.

If the party knew about the Bridge Plane, they might act differently. They might confront the Oracle. They might attempt to prevent the collapse. They might make decisions based on information that is currently locked inside Archie's head.

Archie's silence on this matter may be strategic—he doesn't trust the Guild's interpretation, or he's waiting for the right moment to reveal it. Or it may be paralysis—too many secrets, too much pressure, too many consequences for every possible action.

## The Third Eye — Archie's Deepest Mystery

Archie has a connection to something called 'the Third Eye' that Waluigi does not fully understand.

The Third Eye Circlet—found by Markop in the Shadow Estate maze—was inscribed with Archie's handwriting: 'The eye sees across—the band keeps me from falling in.' The circlet was Archie's personal safeguard against dimensional fracture. He encountered his own TWO-EYED CLONE in the sewers beneath a restaurant—a clone desperate to steal his third eye for the Iron Legion's necromancers.

The circlet kept Archie anchored during his escape through 'Deep Layers' and prevented the Oracle's fractured visions from consuming him during the Shattered Ritual.

Marcus Ashfold—Orangus Cornelius's military consultant—mentioned 'keeping an eye on the three ey—' before cutting himself off. The Third Eye is significant. Multiple parties are interested in it. And Archie is at the center of whatever it represents.

Waluigi does not have enough information to explain what the Third Eye IS. But Waluigi notes that Archie's magical instability, his entropy-bleeding signature, his dimensional sensitivity, and his connection to the Third Eye may all be related. Archie may not merely be a fire mage who causes problems. He may be a CONDUIT—a living breach in dimensional stability whose very existence weakens the barriers between planes.

If this is true, the Mages' Guild's interest in 'overseeing' Archie is not about control. It's about CONTAINMENT. Archie is not just a weapon they want to aim. He is a hazard they need to manage.

## Archie's Magic — The Entropy Problem

The Guild described Archie's magic as 'bleeding entropy.' This requires examination.

Normal mages cast spells. The spell does its thing. The magic dissipates. The world returns to normal.

Archie casts spells and the world does NOT return to normal. Residual energy leaks from his casting. Dimensional boundaries weaken in his vicinity. Planar instability increases where he has been.

The Planar Fracture was caused by the Oracle's ritual failure and the party's inability to maintain the synchronization array. But Archie's entropy contributed. His magic was the 'unstable foundation' that Waluigi identified as a problem BEFORE the ritual began. When Waluigi raised concerns and was SHUSHED, the concern was specifically about Archie's magic destabilizing the ritual.

Waluigi was RIGHT. The shushing was UNJUSTIFIED. And reality broke.

Archie's entropy-bleeding means that wherever he goes, reality gets slightly weaker. The longer he stays, the worse it gets. Mirrors behave strangely. Shadows fall wrong. Dimensional boundaries thin.

This is why the Guild wants him contained. This is why his presence at Raventree Manor—already a nexus of planar fractures—is simultaneously useful and dangerous. His entropy might help destabilize ghosts (making them easier for Luigi to vacuum). It might also destabilize the remaining dimensional barriers (making everything worse).

Archie Miser is a walking planar hazard who also happens to be the Guild's best tool for addressing planar hazards. The contradiction is the point. The Guild doesn't need Archie to be safe. They need him to be AIMED.

## Current Situation — Raventree Manor, Late Harvestide 1040

Archie is currently at Raventree Manor with Luigi, Thornbury, Agent L, and various Guild operatives. His stated mission is ghost-clearing. His actual situation is far more complicated:

- He owes 2,062 gold to the Guild for a broken rope
- He works for the Guild under coercion, not choice
- His magic bleeds entropy that destabilizes the manor further
- He carries secrets about Toadburt and the Bridge Plane
- His possessions were stolen by a singing fortune teller who used them to open a portal
- He heard the Guild discuss his acceptable death
- He is separated from most of Disaster Inc.
- His Third Eye connection makes him a target for multiple factions
- Bryan the Toad, Dan, and Purple T are actively HUNTING him, entering through planar portals with intentions ranging from 'find' to 'capture' to 'possibly kill'

Archie does not know about the hunting party. Bryan—servant of the Toad god—recruited Dan from the Mages' Guild, Purple T opened a planar portal, and they entered the Shadowfell looking for Archie. Their stated intentions include 'revenge' (Dan's, though his commitment seemed forced), divine judgment (Bryan's), and whatever Purple T considers entertainment.

The hunting party encountered Mazebounds, scorncrows, blood fountains, and eventually a massive fireball that set the grove ablaze—suggesting someone with significant fire magic was nearby. Whether this was Archie or another entity is unclear.

## Waluigi's Assessment — The Archie Problem

Archie Miser is exhausted. Hunted by rogue Guild operatives. Carrying the weight of multiple secrets. Employed by an organization that considers his death an acceptable outcome. Bleeding dimensional instability from his very existence. Financially destroyed. Separated from most allies. Targeted by a vengeful hunting party he doesn't know about.

And yet.

Archie survived the Shadowfell. A MONTH in the plane of shadow, alone, without his fire, in a dimension designed to extinguish hope. He survived through disguise, deception, improvisation, and the stubborn refusal to lie down and die that characterizes everyone in Disaster Inc.

He adapted when his fire was taken. He deceived vampires who should have seen through him. He gathered intelligence that nobody else could have obtained. He learned truths about Toadburt and the Oracle that may prove crucial to resolving the crisis.

Archie is a problem. Archie causes problems. Archie IS a problem in the most fundamental sense—his existence destabilizes reality.

But Archie is ALIVE. And in the current crisis, where so many are dead or missing or worse, being alive and operational counts for more than being perfect.

Waluigi advises standing even further away from Archie now than before. The entropy, the secrets, the stress, the hunting parties, the Guild coercion, the dimensional instability—all of it is building toward a discharge point. When Archie's accumulated pressure finally releases, Waluigi wants to be at MINIMUM safe distance.

Because when Archie goes off, he goes off like a fireball in a wooden ship. The intentions don't matter. The precision doesn't exist. Everything within range gets burned.

Everything within range ALWAYS gets burned.

Stress makes Archie combustible. And Archie has never been under more stress than he is right now.

WAH.

Archie is described by friends and enemies alike as a man of action and consequences. He is a 'flamethrower' in more ways than one, often leaving destruction in his wake, even when his intentions are constructive. 

## The Letter of Fate
A recovered letter from a friend (who owes him for some rope) reveals that Archie is viewed as a pivotal figure in the Shadowfell. He is warned not to trust mirrors or the silence after screaming stops. His connection to the 'Shadowfell feeds on guilt' suggests a man burdened by his past actions. 

## Equipment
Archie is known for his watch—a sealed inventory that tracks more than just time. Its return to the group via Tymnas is a sign that Archie is either nearby or being used as a lure to draw the others into the 'Orange Deer' shrine in the grove.

description:
## A Family Larger Than a Bloodline

The Bone-Line Registry uses family more broadly than genealogy. Sans and Papyrus are its best-known brothers, but the household includes elders, working cousins, young dependents, adopted guests, and several unresolved figures connected to Underground science.

## Snowdin’s Safety Net

Papyrus welcomes strangers, Will keeps supplies, Dirty Brother maintains the heat, and the wider household keeps food and beds ready when Snowdin’s roads become unsafe. Their humor is not a refusal to take danger seriously; it is how they make danger survivable.

## Sans’s Place

Sans is not the official leader. He is the quiet sentry who notices danger before it reaches the door and trusts the rest of the Bone-Line to make the home worth defending.
